Who we are:
Shape a brighter financial future with us.
Together with our members, we’re changing the way people think about and interact with personal finance.
We’re a next-generation financial services company and national bank using innovative, mobile-first technology to help our millions of members reach their goals. The industry is going through an unprecedented transformation, and we’re at the forefront. We’re proud to come to work every day knowing that what we do has a direct impact on people’s lives, with our core values guiding us every step of the way. Join us to invest in yourself, your career, and the financial world.
The role:
As the Fraud and Disputes Member Treatment & Operations Lead, you will own the design and evolution of how SoFi protects, communicates with, supports, restricts, and resolves member experiences across fraud and disputes.
You will define clear, risk-informed treatment principles and translate them into operating requirements that teams can execute consistently across products, channels, and fraud scenarios.
You will serve as the connective layer across Fraud and Disputes Operations, Risk Strategy, Product, Engineering, Legal, Compliance, and Communications—resolving complex tradeoffs among loss prevention, member protection, fairness, operational feasibility, and long-term member trust.
In this role, success is not just about policy or process. It is about ensuring that members receive timely, clear, and consistent treatment when they need SoFi most, while maintaining strong controls and scalable operational execution.
What you’ll do:
Own Member Treatment Design (30%): Define and maintain end-to-end member-treatment principles across fraud and disputes, including segmentation, decision principles, restrictions, escalation paths, resolution experiences, and channel consistency.
Set treatment guardrails for high-impact decisions, ensuring member communications, frontline actions, and risk controls are timely, consistent, and defensible.
Translate Strategy into Operational Execution (25%): Convert fraud, disputes, policy, and regulatory requirements into clear operating standards for processes, communications, training, tooling, quality controls, and measurement.
Lead readiness for material treatment changes and emerging fraud events, aligning containment actions, member messaging, escalation pathways, and post-incident remediation.
Lead Cross-Functional Treatment Design (20%): Partner with Product, Engineering, Risk, Legal, Compliance, and Operations to define requirements for member-facing journeys, workflow, decisioning, agent tooling, and exception handling.
Facilitate design reviews and resolve complex tradeoffs across fraud types, products, channels, and member segments.
Own Member Communications and Scam Education (15%): Set the approach for fraud- and scam-related communications, including prevention education, in-product messaging, agent guidance, and post-incident outreach.
Use scam trends, member contacts, complaints, and engagement data to prioritize education campaigns and improve message effectiveness.
Establish Governance and Continuous Improvement (10%): Set decision rights, approval paths, and documentation for treatment changes and exceptions.
Use operational, risk, quality, complaints, contact-driver, and member-experience data to identify treatment gaps, quantify impact, and prioritize durable improvements.
What you’ll need:
• BA/BS degree required or equivalent practical experience.
• 12+ years of experience in fraud, risk, disputes, member experience, operations strategy, product operations, or related financial-services work.
• Deep knowledge of fraud and member-treatment practices in a regulated environment.
• Demonstrated success leading complex, companywide programs or operating processes through indirect influence.
• Ability to synthesize policy, data, operational realities, and regulatory expectations into clear recommendations and executable requirements.
• Experience evaluating member impacts of fraud controls, decisioning, restrictions, investigations, and resolution processes.
• Strong executive communication skills, judgment, and ability to resolve ambiguous, high-impact tradeoffs.
• Experience partnering with Product, Engineering, Legal, Compliance, and Operations on member-facing changes.
• Highly motivated self-starter with the ability to build alignment in a fast-paced, dynamic environment.
Nice to have:
• Experience across multiple fraud domains, including identity, scams, transaction fraud, first-party fraud, or disputes.
• Experience with journey design, decisioning, controls, complaints, or regulatory remediation.
• Experience designing member communications, prevention education, or agent guidance for high-risk or high-friction moments.

Identify and Resolve Control and Process Gaps (20%): Evaluate fraud-prevention processes, identify systemic control gaps, quantify operational and financial exposure, and prioritize durable remediation across ATO, identity risk, and scam typologies.
Lead root-cause analysis of material fraud incidents, emerging attack patterns, control failures, and member-impacting defects; convert findings into clear control, workflow, training, and communication changes.

Provide risk-based recommendations and resolve tradeoffs among fraud exposure, member impact, operational feasibility, and control effectiveness in partnership with cross-functional stakeholders.

• Demonstrated expertise in sophisticated fraud attack methodologies, identity fraud, authentication, and scam prevention.
• Advanced understanding of fraud-detection technologies, authentication frameworks, identity-verification solutions, case-management platforms, and the operational application of fraud rules and risk models.
• Ability to analyze data, weigh risk and member impact, and make high-judgment recommendations.
• Strong influence, program-management, and written and verbal communication skills.
• Demonstrated ability to translate fraud strategy, policies, and regulatory requirements into scalable operational processes and controls.
• Experience leading cross-functional work across Operations, Product, Engineering, Risk, Legal, Compliance, and Controls.

• Experience in a highly regulated consumer financial-services environment.

Why join us
Brex is the intelligent finance platform that enables companies to spend smarter and move faster in more than 200 markets. By combining global corporate cards and banking with intuitive spend management, bill pay, and travel software, Brex enables founders and finance teams to accelerate operations, gain real-time visibility, and control spend effortlessly. Brex’s AI-native automation and world-class service eliminate manual expense and accounting tasks for customers so they can focus on what matters most. Tens of thousands of the world's best companies run on Brex, including DoorDash, Coinbase, Robinhood, Zoom, Plaid, Reddit, and SeatGeek.
Working at Brex allows you to push your limits, challenge the status quo, and collaborate with some of the brightest minds in the industry. We’re committed to building a diverse team and inclusive culture and believe your potential should only be limited by how big you can dream. We make this a reality by empowering you with the tools, resources, and support you need to grow your career.
Implementation at Brex
Implementation transforms new customers into power users. We lead the onboarding experience for companies adopting Brex Empower, helping them shift from outdated processes to a modern, employee-first approach. It’s a role that blends customer empathy, project management, technical expertise, process design, and change management. We take personal ownership of our customers' long-term success, and we set customers up thoroughly so they can be with ‘Brex for life’. As strategic advisors, we build trust, drive solutions with tenacity, deliver results fast, and work cross-functionally to make adoption seamless for customers.
What you’ll do
Embedded is Brex's most strategically important growth frontier and this role sits at the epicenter. You'll sit on the Implementation Team and will wire together partner ecosystems across Business Development and Product, configure complex integrations, and deliver customer experiences that genuinely delight. You won't be following a playbook, you’ll be writing it. This role focuses on ensuring successful onboarding and configuration of embedded services such as Navan, Zip, Coupa Cards, and ICCP partnerships
Where you’ll work
This role will be based in our Seattle office. We are a hybrid environment that combines the energy and connections of being in the office with the benefits and flexibility of working from home. We currently require a minimum of three coordinated days in the office per week, Monday, Wednesday and Thursday. As a perk, we also have up to four weeks per year of fully remote work!
Responsibilities
• Lead implementation workstreams for embedded services across all customer segments
• Own end-to-end implementation for embedded-only customer projects. Partner with the BD team on net-new embedded partnership launches helping define how Brex integrates with the next generation of platforms.
• Configure embedded services in coordination with partner tech specs and Brex.
• Provide consultative guidance to customers to ensure embedded tools are correctly deployed.
• Maintain deep knowledge of embedded product evolution and serve as the internal authority, educating CSMs, VIP Support, and cross-functional teams.
Requirements
• Experience: 2-4+ years in a SaaS customer facing role
• Domain Knowledge: Familiarity with embedded finance or third-party SaaS integrations you understand how these ecosystems fit together and where friction hides.
• Communication: A natural communicator who can translate technical complexity into clear, confident guidance for Brex customers, partners, and internal stakeholders.
• Execution: Highly organized and comfortable managing multiple concurrent projects in a fast-moving environment where no two implementations look the same.
• Mindset: Energized by ambiguity. You thrive when the product is evolving and the partnership landscape is expanding.
Bonus points
• Experience in Financial, Expense Management, or ERP software.
• Familiarity with any of the following domains: General Ledger, Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, Billing, Expense Management, Travel, Procurement, or Corporate Card programs.
Compensation
The expected salary range for this role is $119,328 - $181,930 USD. However, the starting base pay will depend on a number of factors including the candidate’s location, skills, experience, market demands, and internal pay parity. Depending on the position offered, equity and other forms of compensation may be provided as part of a total compensation package.
Brex LLC is a wholly owned subsidiary of Capital One, N.A.

• Self-motivated and able to run with projects autonomously with minimal oversight

• Strong sense of ownership, taking responsibility for results and driving issues to resolution

The Product team is at the forefront of Brex's mission to empower employees anywhere to make better financial decisions. With a deep understanding of the business, we identify and scope the most impactful opportunities for Brex to tackle. We align cross-functional teams—including Engineering, Legal, Compliance, and Design—on key decisions, set strategy, and drive products from inception to launch.
What you’ll do
Processing a single expense is becoming commoditized. Managing expenses across an enterprise is not. Companies must distribute cards broadly while controlling risk, documenting transactions, enforcing policy, routing approvals, preparing for audit, and producing ERP-ready records.
As Senior Product Manager for Expenses, you will turn that complexity into one intelligent system for employees, managers, finance teams, and accountants. You will lead the strategy across documentation, policy, compliance, approvals, substantiation, audit, and accounting readiness.
You will align specialized product teams across Engineering, Design, Risk, Compliance, Accounting, and GTM. Using AI and automation, you will eliminate routine work, surface meaningful exceptions, help finance teams close faster, and build capabilities that win major enterprise relationships.
Where you’ll work
This role will be based in either our San Francisco, Seattle, or New York office. We are a hybrid environment that combines the energy and connections of being in the office with the benefits and flexibility of working from home. We currently require a minimum of three coordinated days in the office per week, Monday, Wednesday and Thursday. As a perk, we also have up to four weeks per year of fully remote work!
Responsibilities
• Own the end-to-end strategy for enterprise expense management.
• Unify documentation, policy, compliance, approvals, substantiation, audit, and ERP readiness.
• Define the systems, data models, configurations, and controls complex enterprises require.
• Align specialized product teams around the complete expense lifecycle.
• Use AI to automate routine work and route only judgment-heavy exceptions to people.
• Partner with Design to make sophisticated enterprise workflows intuitive.
• Align Engineering, Design, Risk, Compliance, Accounting, Sales, and Customer Success around enterprise outcomes.
• Own adoption, workflow completion, manual-work reduction, close speed, retention, and software revenue.
Requirements
• A track record of leading complex enterprise workflow or systems products.
• Strong technical fluency in backend systems, data models, integrations, and configurable product architecture.
• Experience supporting extensive customer permutations without sacrificing usability.
• Ability to unite multiple domains under one strategy and operating model.
• Strong customer and Design judgment across employee, manager, finance, and accounting experiences.
• Concrete judgment about where AI should remove work and where human review matters.
• Strong cross-functional influence and an understanding of how product capabilities affect enterprise sales and adoption.
• Expense management experience is preferred; accounting, ERP, procurement, compliance, or adjacent enterprise-software experience can substitute.
Compensation
The expected salary range for this role is $184,000 - $230,000. However, the starting base pay will depend on a number of factors including the candidate’s location, skills, experience, market demands, and internal pay parity. 52 million Americans own crypto, and they skew younger, more diverse, and more digitally engaged. Coinbase is building the platform for the onchain economy, from crypto trading to tokenized stocks, prediction markets, and beyond. The Brand Partnerships team meets this audience where they already are, partnering with premium sports, gaming, and lifestyle properties to build cultural relevance and shift brand perception through activations that feel unconventional yet native. As a Brand Partnership Associate - esports, Gaming & Internet Culture, you'll own the coordination and operational execution across Coinbase’s gaming and crypto portfolio, including partnerships with Riot Games, Polytopia, and gaming and crypto-native creators, managing timelines, partner deliverables, and activation logistics.
What you’ll do:
• Develop and maintain relationships with key gaming partners and support the Sr. Manager and cross-functional teams on brand initiatives leveraging the gaming and creator portfolio.
• Own asset inventories, activation trackers, and timeline management for Riot Games, Polytopia, and gaming and crypto-native creator partnerships, and maintain a tracker for emerging pilot opportunities.
• Lead day-to-day project management for gaming activations, including weekly status updates, meeting notes, creative approvals, partner follow-ups, and coordination with external partners.
• Support GTM strategy and briefing/ideation for marquee moments like Worlds and Champs, and build mid-season and end-of-season recaps.
• Surface and track emerging gaming, esports, and internet culture experiments and unofficial partnership opportunities for senior leadership.
• Drive budget tracker upkeep, purchase order processing, and invoice reconciliation across the sports portfolio.
Required Skills and Experience:
• 2+ years of experience in esports, gaming marketing, and/or creator/influencer marketing partnerships.
• Demonstrated ability to manage multiple concurrent project timelines, deliverables, and external partner relationships simultaneously.
• Hands-on experience coordinating with agencies and creators, including managing briefs, content approvals, deliverables, and posting schedules.
• Proven success working cross-functionally with creative, social, communications, and analytics teams to deliver activations on time.
• Familiarity with the gaming, esports, or internet culture ecosystem, including publishers, tournament organizers, streaming platforms, and creator networks.
• A pulse on emerging gaming, internet and crypto culture trends, with a track record of identifying moments early and connecting them to brand opportunities. Agency-side experience in gaming partnerships is a plus.
• Utilizes generative AI responsibly, maintaining human oversight to deliver business-ready outputs and drive measurable improvements in workflow efficiency, cost, and quality.

We oversee all financial aspects of Robinhood's core trading and net interest products in Brokerage, including equities, options, margin lending, securities lending, uninvested cash and more across self-directed, managed, and institutional accounts. We also serve as the finance partner to Robinhood's Platforms organizations: Customer Experience, Customer Trust & Safety, Financial Crimes, and Fraud Operations. These volume-driven teams protect our customers and keep the platform running for every business at Robinhood, and their scope reaches well beyond Brokerage.
As the Finance & Strategy Senior Manager for Platforms, you will be the senior finance lead and primary thought partner to the leaders of these organizations. You will own the end-to-end financial picture for teams whose cost base moves with customer volume, market activity, and product launches: translating contact, case, and alert volumes into headcount and vendor capacity, forecasting fraud and operational losses, setting and defending expense and efficiency targets, and shaping the investment case for automation and tooling. You will set the agenda for how Finance supports these businesses, and you will be the person leadership turns to when they need a clear point of view on what a decision costs, what it saves, and what risk it carries.
The ideal candidate has done this before: a seasoned Finance & Strategy or business finance leader who has covered customer-facing, operations-heavy organizations (support, trust and safety, fraud, risk operations) at a fintech or consumer technology company, and who is fluent in volume-based capacity planning and vendor economics. You operate independently, navigate ambiguity, and drive senior business leaders to decisions. This role has regular exposure to Robinhood's executive team and requires exceptional communication skills and executive presence.
This role is based in our Menlo Park, CA office, with in-person attendance expected at least 3 days per week.

• Own the forecast and analysis of fraud and operational losses, partnering with Fraud, Risk, and Accounting on loss drivers, reserves, and the tradeoff between loss rates, control tightness, and customer friction
• Define and track unit economics and efficiency metrics such as cost per contact, cost per case or alert, cost to serve per customer, loss rates, and deflection rates, and set targets that hold up under volume swings

• Partner with Workforce Management, Procurement, Accounting, and People teams so forecasts are grounded in operational reality and actuals are clean and auditable

• Expert financial modeling skills and the judgment to balance precision with speed; strong grasp of accounting concepts and what makes a model auditable
• Outstanding written and verbal communication; comfortable presenting to executives and simplifying complex tradeoffs
• Mastery of Google Sheets, Excel, Google Slides, and PowerPoint; proficiency with SQL and BI tools (Superset, Looker) and planning software (Anaplan) strongly preferred
• Proven ability to manage multiple competing priorities and drive projects to completion with minimal direction
• A positive attitude. This means a desire to work hard, be creative, stay curious, and maintain a can-do approach
• Experience in fintech, brokerage, payments, or consumer technology; exposure to regulated environments is a plus
• Strong project management skills and the ability to execute collaboratively across complex, matrixed environments

In 1933, Harry Beck introduced a radically different map of the London Underground. Rather than faithfully depicting the geography of London, he simplified the sprawling transit network into clean lines, clear connections, and a system that anyone could navigate. Distances were distorted, angles were standardized, and unnecessary details disappeared. The result was something far more useful than a geographically accurate map: a way for millions of people to understand a complex system and confidently find their way through it.
Beck understood something fundamental. The best way to explain something complicated isn't to show people everything. It's to understand what matters to them and make that unmistakably clear.
At Mercury, we believe great product marketing works the same way. Banking* and payments can be complex, but the value they create for customers shouldn't be. Our job is to understand what people need, find the essence of what we're building, and help customers see how it can make their lives better.
We're a financial technology company building products that help ambitious businesses do more with their money. From everyday banking and payments to international money movement and emerging capabilities like agentic payments, we're making complex financial workflows feel remarkably simple.
We're looking for a Product Marketing Manager to help bring these products to market, communicate their value, and make sure customers discover and use what we're building.
This role sits at the intersection of Product, Marketing, and Revenue. You'll develop positioning, lead go-to-market strategies, drive successful product launches, and identify opportunities to increase adoption and revenue.
We care deeply about craft, but successful product marketing is about more than a beautiful campaign or a well-executed announcement. It's about understanding customers, building an effective plan, and driving meaningful results.
*Mercury is a fintech company, not an FDIC-insured bank. Banking services provided through Choice Financial Group and Column N.A., Members FDIC.
In this role, you'll:
• Lead impactful product launches. Own end-to-end go-to-market strategy and execution for new banking and payments capabilities, including emerging agentic features. Develop launch plans, align cross-functional teams, prepare customer-facing partners, and measure impact on product adoption and business goals.
• Get close to our customers. Build a deep understanding of how founders and finance teams manage money, what challenges they face, and why they choose one financial product over another. Turn these insights into compelling positioning, messaging, and GTM strategies.
• Execute AI-first. Use AI to work smarter, move faster, and produce better outcomes. You’ll build and use existing workflows, automations, and repeatable processes that improve how you approach research, launch execution, competitive intelligence, and other core responsibilities.

• Become an expert on our market. Develop a sharp understanding of the banking and payments competitive landscape, including emerging fintech products and traditional financial institutions. Translate market insights into differentiated positioning and actionable recommendations.
• Equip our Revenue teams to win. Build trusted relationships with customer-facing teams and develop the competitive intelligence, battlecards, messaging, and training they need to communicate Mercury's value confidently and accurately.
• Work with exceptional cross-functional partners. Collaborate with Product, Brand, Creative, Lifecycle, and Revenue to bring go-to-market strategies to life. Help shape strong campaign briefs and channel strategies, drawing on specialized creative expertise when needed.
• Connect marketing to business impact. Define clear objectives for launches and growth initiatives, track meaningful performance indicators, and communicate what worked, what didn't, and what we should do next.

Ramp is hiring a People Strategy, M&A Lead to build a function that doesn't exist here today: how Ramp attracts, evaluates, prices, and closes the teams and companies that join us through an acquisition. This is a new role, and you'll build it from the ground up.

You'll own that work end to end. For team acquisitions, that means the pipeline, the assessment, the economics, the founder and team conversations, the offers, and post-close integration with People Operations and the hiring teams. You'll run the hiring process yourself, from first conversation to signed offers, and stay with the team through post-close integration, which no one owns at Ramp today. The scope will change as we do more of this, and defining it is part of the job.

This role will grow with what Ramp does. As volume grows, so does the scope: larger acquisitions alongside Corporate Development, the people side of company acquisitions, and strategy work across People Finance & Strategy. At Ramp, people who have built deep operating judgment in roles like this have gone on to lead major business areas. Our mission is to transform global finance by empowering professionals at the world's top investment banks, private equity funds, and investment firms with AI that delivers unparalleled speed, accuracy, and insight. We're not just improving financial workflows; we're redefining them.

This is a unique opportunity to join a generational company driving transformation in one of the most important industries in the world. With a rapidly growing, global client base, proven product-market fit, and backing from world-class investors, we are scaling quickly and defining a new category of enterprise AI.

Our team is sharp, motivated, and deeply committed to Rogo’s mission. We take ownership of complex problems and stay relentlessly focused on our users. If you thrive in a fast-paced environment, demand excellence, and want to help build the future of finance, we invite you to join us.

About The Role:

We’re seeking a Strategic Finance Lead to own pricing strategy and the financial side of Deal Desk at Rogo. You will partner with RevOps, Sales, Product, and leadership to connect customer value, go-to-market strategy, product capabilities, and unit economics to how we package, price, and sell.

This hands-on role spans strategic design and live deal execution. You will develop a deep understanding of customers, sales motions, features, and the product roadmap, then shape pricing and commercial strategies that support growth, strong unit economics, and long-term customer value.

What You Will Own:

Pricing Strategy & Monetization

 - Lead pricing and packaging analyses by segment and product, aligning recommendations with customer value, adoption, willingness to pay, and GTM strategy.

 - Partner with Product and GTM on monetizing new features and roadmap investments, including positioning, packaging, launch strategy, and the customer experience.

 - Recommend pricing tests, rollout plans, and success measures.

Financial Forecasting & FP&A

 - Forecast the financial impact of pricing changes, new products, and significant deals, translating commercial assumptions into revenue, cost, and cash flow outcomes.

 - Build and maintain driver-based models that link pipeline, new business, retention, and expansion to the company’s operating model and financial plan.

 - Contribute to the annual plan, forecasts, and long-range planning; track forecasts against actual results, explain variances, and refine assumptions.

 - Develop scenario and sensitivity analyses to inform pricing, investment, and resource allocation decisions.

GTM & Product Partnership

 - Own financial evaluation of complex and nonstandard deals with Sales and RevOps across new business, renewals, and expansions

 - Evaluate commercial proposals and contract terms; assess customer lifetime value (LTV), return on investment (ROI), cash flow, and risk under a range of business scenarios.

 - Develop pricing guardrails and exception frameworks with RevOps, Legal, and Accounting; ensure commercial decisions are operationally feasible and supported by clear approvals.

Unit Economics, Analytics & Decision Support

 - Build customer, product, and segment analyses to understand unit economics, LTV, acquisition efficiency, and ROI

 - Assess how product adoption, feature mix, retention, and cost to serve affect long-term economics; evaluate growth and investment tradeoffs with Product and Engineering.

 - Present clear recommendations to leadership, feed pricing assumptions into forecasts, and revisit decisions against actual outcomes.

Key Qualifications and Experience

Required

 - 8+ years of experience in strategic finance, pricing, commercial finance, investment banking, or investing, including meaningful operating experience in a high-growth technology company.

 - Hands-on experience shaping pricing, packaging, or complex commercial deals in an enterprise technology business.

 - Strong financial modeling and analytical skills, including unit economics, LTV, ROI, and scenario analysis under uncertain growth and cost assumptions.

 - Demonstrated ability to partner with Sales, RevOps, and Product, understand technical product capabilities, and turn analysis into commercially practical decisions.

 - Strong business judgment and communication skills, with the ability to influence stakeholders and balance growth, customer value, and financial discipline.

Preferred

Zip is the AI platform for enterprise procurement — built for humans and agents working together. By orchestrating procurement across teams, tools, and suppliers with the help of AI agents, companies can secure the resources they need to innovate faster than ever before.

The world’s most influential enterprises trust Zip, including T-Mobile, OpenAI, AMD, Mars, Dollar Tree, and more. Together they’ve saved over $8 billion and processed over $500 billion in spend. Zip’s team includes product leaders from Apple, Airbnb, and Meta, as well as former procurement leaders from United Health, Sanofi, MGM Resorts, Discover, and NASA.

Backed by Adams Street, Alkeon, BOND, CRV, DST, Tiger Global, and Y Combinator, Zip has raised $371 million, most recently at a $2.2 billion valuation and has been recognized by Forbes Fintech 50, Fast Company's Most Innovative Companies, Inc. Best in Business, and LinkedIn Top Startups.




YOUR ROLE

Be at the forefront of bringing agentic AI to procurement: automating intake, accelerating approvals, and transforming how enterprises manage spend and vendor decisions at scale.

As an AI FDE, you will partner closely with a small group of enterprise customers to design, build, and deliver high-quality AI agents and AI based products that automate complex procurement workflows. You'll make those first customers successful, turn what works into a repeatable playbook, and train our Solutions Consultants to scale the deployment to the rest of our customers.

This is a high-impact role ideal for someone who thrives at the intersection of customer engagement, solution design, and AI-driven product development.

This track is for procurement leaders who have led sourcing, contracting, intake and approvals, the work our agents automate, and want to shape how AI does it. You don't need to code. You'll work alongside our engineers to turn your procurement judgment into agents customers trust.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Design & Build AI Agents & AI Based Products: Work hand-in-hand with customers to understand procurement workflows and develop AI agents & AI based products that solve their most critical pain points.

 - Plan and Scope Deployments: Set the scope, success criteria and project plan with the initial launch customers before kickoff, then own time to value through go-live.

 - Own the Quality Bar: Write the requirements, test cases and evals, and hold the line on accuracy and reliability before an agent goes live.

 - Feedback Loop into Product: Turn what you learn in the field into requirements and priorities for engineering and product, and guide the roadmap for our AI agent platform.

 - Build the Playbook: Turn what works into a repeatable playbook and train our Solutions Consultants to scale the deployment to more customers.

 - Bring the Procurement Lens: Turn sourcing, contracting and approval best practice into agent skills, policies and test cases, and judge agent output the way a procurement leader would.

 - Thrive in high intensity environments where change and iteration are key to success

 - 4+ years of in-house procurement experience, including implementing procurement tools (ie. Coupa, Ariba etc.)

 - Ownership of a spend portfolio, with software and services deals you negotiated end to end

 - A procurement workflow you designed in a P2P tool, such as intake or PR-to-PO

 - Daily use of AI tools in your own sourcing or contracting work

 - A track record of taking projects from plan to production: setting scope, success criteria and timelines, and delivering against them

 - Experience writing requirements and partnering with engineering and design to ship products

 - A track record of influencing cross-functional partners and leadership without direct authority

 - Ability to prioritize ruthlessly, even if it may disappoint customers or stakeholders

 - Strong written and verbal communication with internal and external stakeholders, including executives

 - Extreme attention to detail, with the ability to quickly grasp complex business processes and industry knowledge

 - Deep technical curiosity with ability to understand and influence how AI agents & AI based products are built, tested, and improved

 - Bonus: Experience with agent-building tools (e.g., n8n, Glean) or familiarity with MCP (Model Context Protocol)

 - Bonus: Contracting and risk reviews for AI vendors, or SOX and audit controls work

 - Bonus: Org-wide training you built and delivered

 - Bonus: Product management experience, or past roles where you worked with end customers to influence software development

 - Bonus: Python or SQL scripting experience

Your customers are Datadog's engineers, Finance team and product managers. You will make complex cost data useful in their daily decisions: what changed, why it changed, what happens next, and what to do about it. You will enable intuitive cost allocation, explanation, and forecasting experiences, and connect internal needs with Datadog's Cloud Cost Management product.
At Datadog, we place value in our office culture - the relationships and collaboration it builds and the creativity it brings to the table. We operate as a hybrid workplace to ensure our Datadogs can create a work-life harmony that best fits them.
What You’ll Do:
• Own discovery, strategy, and prioritization for internal FinOps products. Understand the distinct decisions Engineering, Finance, executives, and PMs need to make, and validate which problems are most valuable to solve.
• Make cost allocation understandable and actionable, including shared-platform costs, service consumption, and product and customer margins. Embed cost views into the core platforms, dashboards, and workflows teams already use.
• Improve the cost-explanation experience so teams can quickly understand cost changes, identify their causes, distinguish ongoing costs from temporary changes, and project timelines for expected cost corrections. Where current processes depend on a mandate, build the product that teams will choose to use, then retire the mandate.
• Make the underlying metrics self-serve so teams track their own costs, and reduce the review to the decisions that need a room.
• Partner with engineering on timely detection, insights, monitors, and alerts, and support the Engineering-ownership program that puts cost explanation on Engineering leaders.

Mixpanel is the leading product intelligence and analytics platform, trusted by more than 29,000 companies to help understand how people use the products they build. The Technology Partnerships team sits in Product and reports to the CPO. We are small, fast, and outcome-oriented - not a program or account mapping factory. Our job is to put Mixpanel in the stack teams use to build software in the AI era: the LLM platforms, the clouds and warehouses, and the tools where builders plan, design and ship. We pick a short list of partners, go deep technically with each, and measure ourselves on product adoption and new users, not co-sell pipeline.

You'll own a set of partnerships end to end with companies like Anthropic, OpenAI, Google Cloud, Snowflake, Figma and Linear. You decide what we do with yours, and you deliver it: the plan, the integration scope, the launch, and the adoption after launch. You'll work hands-on with PMs and engineers on both sides, so you need to understand how the technology works and bring your own point of view on what we should build together. This is a doer role. You won't have a quota or a playbook to run; you will have strategic goals and the room to hit them. This role reports to the Head of Technology Partnerships.

• Own the plan for each of your partners: what we build together, why, in what order, and what result we expect

• Secure the partner's side of every launch: their roadmap slot, their promotion, placement on their surfaces

• Open new relationships with the partners we choose to pursue, from first conversation to a launched integration

• Contribute to partner selection, and support diligence and deal terms on new partnerships
• Design and execute unique playbooks with partners with aligned, committed outcomes; not a rinse and repeat of collateral creation, account mapping and team socialization
• Coordinate with regional Channel and Sales teams when a partnership has a field motion
• Define and evangelize the value proposition with partners; what are we doing together, why and who should care; Product Marketing is there for support, but this is yours to own.

• 8+ years of professional experience, including technical partnerships, partner or solutions engineering, product, or developer relations at a developer tool, data or AI company
• A record of shipping: you've taken a partnership or integration from idea to launch to adoption, and can show the numbers
• Fluency in the modern data stack (Snowflake, Databricks, BigQuery, Supabase) and the AI developer ecosystem (LLM platforms, agentics frameworks, vibe-coding tools, MCP Servers)
• Technically fluent enough to explain how a partner's technology works and what an integration takes, because you've built or shipped one

About the Team
The mission of the AI Engine team is to ground Mixpanel in AI-native foundations, enabling internal teams to deploy capabilities with accelerating speed while providing customers with intelligent, highly context-aware product insights.. The team owns the full MCP stack (server, client, and dynamic client registration), the context engine, Mixpanel's AI quality and evals framework, prompt infrastructure, and AI compliance.
AI Engine serves three customers at once.
• Product builders — the PMs, engineers, and analysts at companies using Mixpanel — experience the platform indirectly, through whether Mixpanel AI gives them trustworthy answers.
• Every internal Mixpanel team shipping an AI feature is a direct customer: when the platform is there, they build with speed and confidence instead of rebuilding foundations from scratch.
• And increasingly, the “user” isn't human at all — it's an agent that depends on the team's context engine, MCP coverage, and quality guarantees to act on a person's behalf.
The team is also its own best customer: every AI feature inside Mixpanel runs on the same substrate shipped to the rest of the company, so the foundation gets tested by Mixpanel's own product teams before anyone else touches it.
About the Role
As Senior Product Manager for AI Engine, you'll own the roadmap for the infrastructure every AI surface at Mixpanel is built on — from MCP and the context engine to the evals framework that defines what “good” means for an AI agent. Your stakeholders are mostly other builders: engineers, PMs on other teams, and increasingly the agents themselves. Your product's success shows up in what it lets other teams ship, not in a single customer-facing feature.
You'll work closely with engineering and design to take the team from MCP parity today toward trusted, autonomous agents — establishing quality baselines, driving adoption of shared infrastructure across the rest of Mixpanel's product org, and making the case, in writing, for where the platform should invest next.
What You'll Do
• Set and evolve the strategy for Mixpanel's AI platform — using adoption data from internal teams, agent usage patterns, and customer signal to decide where the platform should invest next
• Align engineering and design on the highest-leverage substrate work — MCP parity, the context engine, the evals framework, prompt infrastructure — with clear, written plans that hold up under scrutiny
• Work closely with engineering to experiment with and ship new platform capabilities, from MCP tooling to model routing to context memory, without sacrificing the reliability every downstream team depends on
• Define what “quality” means for an AI agent and build the evals, baselines, and dashboards that make it measurable — then track whether what shipped actually moved it
• Drive adoption of shared infrastructure across other product teams — decide the right model (opt-in, mandated standard, or incentive-based) and own the motion that gets teams to build on the platform instead of rebuilding it themselves
• Tell a clear story about platform investments — to engineering leadership, to other PM teams, and eventually to customers — that connects infrastructure work to the business outcomes it unlocks
• Prioritize ruthlessly across a long list of platform bets, balancing unblocking internal teams today against the long-term bet on an external, customer-facing intelligence layer
• Help define the AI compliance and trust standards every team shipping an AI feature at Mixpanel has to meet
What We're Looking For
• 5+ years of hands-on product management experience, including time as a platform, infrastructure, or developer-tools PM
• Comfort being the PM for engineers and other internal teams rather than only end customers — you're energized by a product whose success is measured in what it lets other people build
• An ability to synthesize usage data, agent behavior, and qualitative feedback from internal stakeholders to drive clarity on what the platform should do next
• A track record of developing, articulating, and executing a product strategy that other teams had to align behind, not just your own

• Direct experience working with LLMs, agents, or AI quality/evals — you understand why performing well on a handful of examples isn't the same as being reliable in production

About the Department
Cloudflare helps build a better Internet and the Emerging Technology and Incubation (ETI) team invents, launches, and brings to market new technologies built on Cloudflare's network. ETI makes dozens of bets on the future of the Internet and takes the ones that work to market.
ETI started in 2016 and incubated several of Cloudflare's major product lines, including Zero Trust and the Developer Platform. Today ETI is focused on the agentic Internet: how AI agents find, read, and pay for content and services, and how creators and companies get paid as agents become a larger share of Internet traffic.
Every bet in ETI follows the same loop: test an idea, build the smallest version that tells us something, get real feedback, iterate, and ship. The team moves quickly and works closely with teams across Cloudflare.

• 5+ years of experience in a customer-facing technical role such as Technical Sales, Solutions/Systems Engineering, or a related field.

Who we are
Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.
Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.
About This Team
Samsara’s mission is to increase the safety, efficiency, and sustainability of the operations that power the global economy. In just over 10 years, we’ve grown from 0 to over $2B ARR by staying deeply attuned to customer needs and fostering a culture of internal innovation. With a $60B+ total addressable market spanning industries like manufacturing, logistics, and construction, our potential for growth is immense - especially for our new products.
The New Products Sales Strategy (NPSS) team’s mandate is to own the end-to-end understanding of our business for each of our new products and work with cross-functional executive leadership to set the go-to-market (GTM) strategy for how to grow over the next three years. We identify the strategic levers for growth, align cross-functional teams, and drive towards high impact outcomes. We report to executive and C-level leadership on the health and priorities of each new product and act as trusted advisors and thought partners to our sales and product leaders. Each team member is an expert on their respective product across Samsara’s end-to-end business and is empowered to both identify and drive the levers for the next wave of growth. We’re defined by our insatiable curiosity and our ownership mindset. This is a highly collaborative and cross-functional role with the ability to work seamlessly across dozens of teams to deliver outcomes.
About the role:
Samsara is looking for a Principal Sales Strategy Manager to support several of our new products recently launched in the market to drive towards outcomes that unlock exponential growth. This role acts as the expert on the end-to-end business health and strategy, coordinates a cross-functional pod of dedicated resources, and helps align decision-making to shape an investment strategy across all parts of the business. Anything limiting growth for each new product is in scope to unlock. This role is the trusted thought partner of our sales and product leadership as well as being seen as an expert by our executive leadership team and cross-functional stakeholders.
This role will be embedded in several of our New Product “Pods”: cross-functional teams across Sales, marketing, and product fully dedicated to new product success. This includes our newly launched specialist seller organization (PSS) - AEs compensated exclusively on a given new product. This role will have a portion of their variable compensation tied to new product outcomes (Net New ACV), in place of the normal corporate bonus, with potential for overperformance through accelerators.
The ideal candidate has experience at a high-growth international B2B Saas company, has worked in new product launches (New Product Introduction (NPI), New Product Release (NPR)) and/or GTM strategy for new products post-launch, is extremely action oriented, and is excited by being part of a fast-paced, high growth, high ambition company.
This is a remote position open to candidates residing in the US except Alaska, Austin Metro, Boulder Metro, California, Chicago Metro, Connecticut, Dallas Metro, Denver Metro, Houston Metro, Maryland, Massachusetts, New Jersey, New York, Rhode Island, Seattle Metro, and Washington, D.C.
You should apply if:
• You want to impact the industries that run our world: Your efforts will result in real-world impact – helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, reduce emissions, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.

About Anthropic
Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.
About the role
As an Applied AI team member at Anthropic, you will be a pre-sales architect focused on becoming a trusted technical advisor helping large enterprises understand the value of Claude and paint the vision on how they can successfully integrate and deploy Claude into their technology stack. You'll combine your deep technical expertise with customer-facing skills to architect innovative LLM solutions that address complex business challenges while maintaining our high standards for safety and reliability.
Working closely with our Sales, Product, and Engineering teams, you'll guide customers from initial technical discovery through successful deployment. You'll leverage your expertise to help customers understand Claude's capabilities, develop evals, and design scalable architectures that maximize the value of our AI systems.
Responsibilities:
•
Partner with account executives to deeply understand customer requirements and translate them into technical solutions, ensuring alignment between business objectives and technical implementation
•
Serve as the primary technical advisor to enterprise customers throughout their Claude adoption journey, from discovery to initial evaluation through deployment. You will need to coordinate internally across multiple teams & stakeholders to drive customer success
•
Support customers building with both the Claude API and Claude for Work
•
Create and deliver compelling technical content tailored to different audiences. You will need to be able to spread the gamut from technical deep dives for engineering & development teams up to business value focused conversations with executives
•
Guide technical architecture decisions and help customers integrate Claude effectively into their existing technology stack
•
Help customers develop evaluation frameworks to measure Claude's performance for their specific use cases
•
Identify common integration patterns and contribute insights back to our Product and Engineering teams
•
Travel occasionally to customer sites for workshops, technical deep dives, and relationship building
•
Maintain strong knowledge of the latest developments in LLM capabilities and implementation patterns
You may be a good fit if you have:
•
5+ years of experience in technical customer-facing roles such as Solutions Architect, Sales Engineer, or Technical Account Manager
•
Experience working with enterprise customers, navigating complex buying cycles involving multiple stakeholders
•
Exceptional ability to build relationships with and communicate technical concepts to diverse stakeholders to include C-suite executives, engineering & IT teams, and more
•
Strong technical communication skills with the ability to translate customer requirements between technical and business stakeholders
•
Experience designing scalable cloud architectures and integrating with enterprise systems
•
Comfortable with python
•
Familiarity with common LLM frameworks and tools or a background in machine learning or data science
•
Excitement for engaging in cross-organizational collaboration, working through trade-offs, and balancing competing priorities
•
A love of teaching, mentoring, and helping others succeed
•
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, able to convey complicated topics in easily understandable terms to a diverse set of external and internal stakeholders. You enjoy engaging in cross-organizational collaboration, working through trade-offs, and balancing competing priorities
•
Passion for thinking creatively about how to use technology in a way that is safe and beneficial, and ultimately furthers the goal of advancing safe AI systems
Deadline to apply: None. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis.
Logistics
Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience
Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience
Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position
Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.
Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.
For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act.
We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.
Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.
How we're different
We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.
The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.
Come work with us!
Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Forward Deployed Program Lead
About the team
The Office of the Field CCO works with the Chief Marketing and Chief Revenue Officers of Databricks’ largest customers to redesign how their commercial organizations operate. We build a peer community of CMOs and CROs, partner with them on go-to-market transformation programs, and ensure those programs deliver measurable business results. The work cuts across sales, marketing, field engineering, and partner teams, and it runs on the customer’s own data.
About the role
You will help to shape and lead Databricks’ strategy for driving AI transformations with our customers. You will report directly to the Field CCO.
This is a role with broad scope that will require you to collaborate across the business: you will set how we deliver transformation engagements, select and run our first 10 pilot accounts, and shape the reusable solutions field engineering builds. You will get work done through account teams, field engineering, field marketing, and enablement.
What you’ll do
Shape the reusable solutions
• Decide, with field engineering, which pilot solutions become reusable skills and agents (for example, an account research agent or a pipeline risk review) so the next 10 accounts can deploy in weeks rather than months.
• Own how the pieces fit together into a coherent offering for a CMO or CRO: which components combine for which workflow, and what the customer needs in place to use them.
• Pressure-test field engineering’s designs against real customer workflows and set the acceptance criteria an asset must meet before it goes to the field.
• Collaborate with our AI FDE team, product team, and FE regional leadership on the solutionization of workflows/companions.
Set the delivery model
• Define how a GTM transformation engagement runs from first executive conversation to production: stages, roles across account, field engineering, and professional services teams, entry and exit criteria, and governance.
• Set the standard for account plans on transformation opportunities and review each plan with the account team before it goes to the customer. A strong plan names the executive sponsor, the two or three workflows in scope (for example, pipeline forecasting or campaign attribution), the data required, and the business result being targeted.
Select and run the pilot program
• Define the selection criteria for the first 10 pilot accounts (executive sponsorship, data readiness, commercial potential, willingness to go public) and finalize the list with sales leadership.
• Program-manage the pilots. Set the operating cadence: weekly working sessions with account teams, monthly customer steering committees, and a quarterly review with the Field CCO.
• Define and track the metrics for each pilot. Measure business outcomes such as forecast accuracy, sales cycle length, or cost per qualified lead, alongside workflow adoption and consumption.
• Identify stalled pilots early and escalate with a specific recovery plan.
Build the CMO and CRO community
• Partner with field marketing to launch and run CMO and CRO councils across North America and EMEA: membership criteria, agenda, and a format that gives members a reason to return.
• Partner with the Office of the CMO on thought leadership for flagship events such as Data + AI Summit and executive dinners, including keynote narratives, customer case studies drawn from the pilots, and point-of-view papers on how commercial organizations are changing.
Enable the field
• Partner with ops and the enablement team to build the mechanisms that teach field engineers and sellers how the solutions work, when to position them, and how to deploy them: playbooks, demo environments, certification paths, and deal reviews.
Minimum Qualifications
• Education: Bachelor's degree in a technical or related field, or equivalent professional experience.
• Experience: 5-7+ years in product development of highly technical products, product operations, GTM strategy, business operations, technical program management, or deploying technical/AI solutions with customers.
• Cross-Organizational Execution: 4+ years collaborating on cross-functional programs that drive committed outcomes across Product, Field Engineering, and Marketing, including at the executive level.
• Communication: Ability to communicate technical concepts to both non-technical and technically proficient audiences, including tailoring messages for potential customers and executives.
• AI & Automation: Demonstrated and creative use of AI-driven tooling and automated workflows.
• Sales/Marketing Expertise: Experience building or working with MarTech/SalesTech, including an understanding of marketing workflows, MMM, MROI, and GTM ontologies.
Preferred Qualifications
• Hands-On AI Agent Deployment: Direct experience scoping, deploying, or evaluating AI agents or predictive analytics workflows (experience with product development for AI agents a plus).
• Some coding experience with React, TypeScript, SQL, or Go.
• MBA or equivalent professional experience.
• Experience with customer-facing strategy , GTM strategy, or value engineering at a high-growth data or AI software company (experience interfacing with end customers to influence software development preferred).

• Own outcomes for a portfolio of strategic customers deploying Fin. Understand their business, their support operation, and their technical environment well enough that the deployment plan you propose earns trust immediately.
• Run the full arc yourself. Pitch and demo Fin, scope the solution, hands-on configure it (including custom development if required), and unblock whatever gets in the way, whether that's a product gap, a technical integration, or a cross-functional snag.
• Be the AI expert in the room. Customers should leave every conversation with you knowing more about how to get outstanding results from Fin.
• Partner tightly with Sales, Success, and R&D so each deployment feels like one team to the customer, not a relay race.
• Turn what you learn in the field into product. Bring specific, evidence-backed input, not just feature requests, to shape the roadmap.
• Build the playbook as you go: the deployment patterns, templates, and best practices that make the next ten deployments faster than the first.
• Help define what Forward Deployed PM means at Fin . It's a very novel role across the industry, still being shaped, and you'll help sharpen what it looks like here.
Success in this role looks like your customers thriving with Fin, and the product getting sharper because of what you learned from them. It's product management at its core, not solutions engineering, customer success, or professional services.
What skills do I need?
• Experience: No minimum years required. We care about impact, drive, and potential, evidenced through the skills below, not tenure.
• Customer obsession: Deep empathy paired with a bias for action. You're motivated by solving the real problem and delivering measurable results.
• Communication & storytelling: You can pitch Fin to a room of executives, then get into the technical weeds with their engineers, adjusting depth and tone without losing either audience.
• Technical fluency: You're able to talk to engineers and customers about modern tech stack, from APIs and SaaS infrastructure to LLMs and low-code tooling. You're comfortable onboarding a customer into more technical product setups.

• Cross-functional influence: You navigate organizational boundaries easily, and bring people together to get the best outcome for customers and Fin.
• Comfort with ambiguity: You thrive in fast-changing, undefined environments, switching fluidly between big-picture strategy and in-the-weeds execution.
• Operational rigor: Operational rigor: You're highly organized and structured, managing multiple deployments and priorities without becoming reactive, and you know when a moment calls for speed versus polish.
Even better if you have:
• Experience building product for enterprise customers
• Startup or B2B SaaS experience
• Background in technical consulting, solutions engineering, or customer success

• Build the playbook as you go: the deployment patterns, templates, and best practices that make the next ten deployments faster than the first.
• Help define what Forward Deployed PM means at Fin . It's a very novel role across the industry, still being shaped, and you'll help sharpen what it looks like here.
Success in this role looks like your customers thriving with Fin, and the product getting sharper because of what you learned from them. It's product management at its core, not solutions engineering, customer success, or professional services.
What skills do I need?
• Experience: No minimum years required. We care about impact, drive, and potential, evidenced through the skills below, not tenure.
• Customer obsession: Deep empathy paired with a bias for action. You're motivated by solving the real problem and delivering measurable results.
• Communication & storytelling: You can pitch Fin to a room of executives, then get into the technical weeds with their engineers, adjusting depth and tone without losing either audience.
• Technical fluency: You're able to talk to engineers and customers about modern tech stack, from APIs and SaaS infrastructure to LLMs and low-code tooling. You're comfortable onboarding a customer into more technical product setups.
• Evidence-based thinking: You use data, not anecdotes, to make the case for a deployment plan or a roadmap bet, and you're comfortable pulling and interpreting data (conversation logs, usage, CX metrics) to find the story.
• Cross-functional influence: You navigate organizational boundaries easily, and bring people together to get the best outcome for customers and Fin.
• Comfort with ambiguity: You thrive in fast-changing, undefined environments, switching fluidly between big-picture strategy and in-the-weeds execution.
• Operational rigor: Operational rigor: You're highly organized and structured, managing multiple deployments and priorities without becoming reactive, and you know when a moment calls for speed versus polish.
Even better if you have:
• Experience building product for enterprise customers
• Startup or B2B SaaS experience
• Background in technical consulting, solutions engineering, or customer success

About the Role
Fivetran is building data pipelines to power the modern data stack for thousands of companies.
Every production dbt pipeline depends on orchestration. When a job runs late, fails without anyone noticing, or gets stuck in a queue, the people downstream stop trusting the data. As Senior Product Manager for Orchestration, you will own how dbt runs in production: how jobs are scheduled and triggered, how they recover when something goes wrong, and how teams find out and fix it.
You will own the vision, roadmap, and outcomes for orchestration on the dbt platform. That covers the job scheduler, triggers and job chaining, retries and run reliability, concurrency and queueing, jobs as code, run monitoring, and notifications. Data teams of every size depend on these systems every day, from a single nightly job to enterprise deployments with hundreds of interdependent jobs across many projects.
You will work closely with the engineering teams behind the scheduler and the v2 engine, with the dbt State team, and with Fivetran’s platform teams as data movement and transformation come together. You will also help define what orchestration looks like as AI agents begin to trigger, monitor, and fix pipelines alongside people. We are looking for someone who is technical, close to customers, and excited by reliability problems: a PM who wants to make the dbt Platform the best place to run dbt in production.
This is a full-time position based out of our Denver office. Our hybrid work model offers a blend of remote flexibility and in-person collaboration, including two days in the office each week to connect and build as a team.
What You’ll Do
•
Own the orchestration strategy and roadmap
•
Define and own the vision and roadmap for dbt platform orchestration, including scheduling, event- and API-based triggers, chaining across jobs and projects, retries, concurrency and queueing, and jobs as code. Turn that vision into clear priorities, sequencing, and tradeoffs.
•
Set success metrics for run reliability, on-time delivery, and time to recovery, and hold yourself accountable for moving them.
•
Decide where to invest, what to build, and what not to build, using customer evidence, usage data, and technical judgment.
•
Make production dbt reliable and observable
•
Partner with engineering to improve run reliability: fewer failed or stuck runs, clearer classification of what went wrong, and faster recovery when it does.
•
Own notifications and run monitoring across email, Slack, webhooks, and integrations, so teams hear about failures quickly, understand what broke, and know what to do next.
•
Work with the v2 and dbt State teams to make sure jobs build only what they need to, and stay fast and cost-efficient at scale.
•
Drive cross-functional execution
•
Lead engineering and design through a predictable shipping cadence, with crisp feature briefs and PRDs that keep teams aligned on what matters and why.
•
Partner with Fivetran platform teams on a connected experience for scheduling and running pipelines across data movement and transformation.
•
Equip Product Marketing, Sales, Solutions Architects, and Support with clear positioning, launch materials, and guidance, including how dbt orchestration compares to standalone orchestrators.
•
Stay close to users and the market
•
Build tight feedback loops with customers who run dbt in production, from small analytics teams to large enterprises, and with teams that orchestrate dbt from tools like Airflow, Dagster, and Prefect.
•
Use usage data, support trends, and customer conversations to find the biggest sources of pain, size them, and bring that evidence into planning.
Skills We’re Looking For
•
5+ years of product management experience, ideally on developer tools, data infrastructure, or platform products.
•
Experience with workflow orchestration or scheduling systems, as a builder or a heavy user (for example Airflow, Dagster, Prefect, or an in-house scheduler).
•
A strong technical foundation: you can reason about distributed systems, queues, and reliability tradeoffs, and engage deeply with engineers on technical decisions.
•
Hands-on experience with dbt for analytics engineering.
•
A quantitative approach: you enjoy digging into usage and reliability data and connecting it to strategy.
•
A track record of shipping in close partnership with engineering and design, and influencing stakeholders without authority.
•
Excellent written and verbal communication, from crisp specs to executive-level narratives.
•
Comfort working asynchronously on a distributed, remote team.
Bonus Skills​
•
Experience building observability, alerting, or incident management products.
•
Experience with CI/CD and Git-based workflows (GitHub, GitLab) or infrastructure as code (for example Terraform).
•
Knowledge of modern data warehouses (Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks, Redshift) and the analytics engineering ecosystem.
•
Experience with Fivetran or other data movement and ELT tools.
•
Hands-on experience using AI agents in your own workflow, and opinions about how they should interact with production systems.

PARTNERSHIPS ENABLEMENT 

ABOUT THE ROLE

Clay works with hundreds of Solutions Partners. These are agencies and firms that sell and implement Clay for their own clients: RevOps and marketing ops agencies, GTM consultancies, systems integrators, and private equity firms. Partners already do most of the services work around Clay, and they bring us a lot of pipeline.

We want every partner to sell Clay as well as our own GTM Engineers do, and to implement it as well as our own team would. You’ll own partner enablement at Clay and focus on two things:

 - Selling Clay. Teach partners how to talk about Clay with their clients: the main use cases, how we compare to other tools, how we connect to the tools they already use, and how Clay fits with the services they sell.

 - Delivering Clay well. Set a clear standard for good Clay work and certify partners against it. Our Sales and GS teams, and our customers, should be able to tell which partners can deliver which use cases.

You’ll build the training and certification, and you’ll also teach it yourself, often in person at partner workshops. You’ll be on our Enablement team and work closely with our Partnerships team. Enablement already has content and systems you can use, so you won’t be starting from zero.

Why this role matters: When partners do great work, customers get more out of Clay and spend more. Partners can do that work at a lower cost than if we hired more of our own people. Partners also send us new customers. Better training makes all of this work better.




WHAT YOU’LL DO



HELP PARTNERS SELL CLAY

 - Teach partners what our GTM Engineers know: use cases, competitors, integrations, and how to pitch Clay to buyers

 - Show partners how Clay helps grow their own services business, not just their clients’

 - Give partners what they need for sales calls with our team, like demo flows, scoping guides, and ROI examples


SET THE STANDARD FOR DELIVERY

 - Work with our delivery and Applied AI teams to define what good Clay work looks like for the most common partner use cases

 - Build certifications for both individuals and partner firms, and make them hard enough to mean something

 - Help our GTM Engineers and GS teams know which partners to bring into deals, and why


BUILD THE PROGRAM AND GROW IT

 - Start with the basics: partner onboarding, a regular product update for partners, and courses in our LMS

 - Run workshops for partners, in person and online, for both technical and newer partners

 - Turn what works into a repeatable program, like a standard onboarding workshop and quarterly sessions, so you can reach hundreds of partners

 - Track certification rates, deals with partners attached, and delivery quality, and use the numbers to improve the program
   



WHAT YOU’LL BRING

 - 5–7+ years in enablement, partner enablement, or a technical customer-facing role like Sales Engineer or Solutions Architect

 - Strong technical skills. You’re comfortable building in GTM data and automation tools, and you can tell good implementation work from bad

 - When someone asks how to do something, you find out what problem they’re really trying to solve

 - You’re a great teacher. You can explain technical topics to a mixed group, from experienced builders to people new to the field

 - You’ve built programs from scratch without a big team or existing systems, and you’re comfortable when things aren’t fully defined

 - You care more about building and teaching than about earning commission

 - You’re happy to travel often to meet partners in person


NICE TO HAVE

 - You’ve used Clay, or worked at an agency that uses Clay

 - You’ve worked on a services or delivery partner program at a company that sells with partners

 - You’ve built a certification or test that partners had to pass

Across GTM, we’re transforming the way we work with AI. We expect every seller, CSM, and team member to become a power user, using it daily to work smarter and move faster.
