Job Description:
Building trusted markets — powered by our people
At Cboe Global Markets, we inspire our people to solve complex challenges together because what we do matters. We provide the financial infrastructure that powers the global economy. As a leading provider of market infrastructure and tradable products, Cboe delivers cutting-edge trading, clearing and investment solutions to market participants around the world.
We're building meaningful ways to support professional and personal development while strengthening the trust we've earned as a global market leader. Our teams are empowered to share ideas, actively pursue them and bring on a challenge. As champions of internal mobility and access to opportunity, we encourage our people to “go for it” and equip our managers with the training to coach their teams to the next level. We strive to provide employees a safe space to network, share ideas and create opportunities.
To support strong partnership and team connection, this role follows a four day in office work model.
Location Overview
Cboe HQ is located in the historic Old Post Office district, it's a landmark that blends classic architecture with modern amenities. The building features expansive spaces with high ceilings and large windows, offering an abundance of natural light and panoramic views of the city skyline and the Chicago River.
With its prime location in the heart of downtown, the OPO Building provides easy access to major transportation hubs, including Union Station and multiple CTA lines, making it convenient for commuters. The building is home to a variety of amenities, including restaurants, a fitness center, and collaborative workspaces, creating a vibrant and dynamic work environment in one of Chicago's most iconic areas.
Position overview
Cboe Global Markets is seeking a Senior Manager, Administrative Support to lead and develop the Executive Assistant team that supports senior leaders across the organization, while also serving as the dedicated Executive Assistant to an assigned senior executive. This is a player-coach role: you will set the standard for executive support at Cboe by delivering it yourself every day and by building a high-performing, well-coordinated team around you.
Reporting to the Senior Director, Facilities, you will own the day-to-day management of the Executive Assistant team, ensure consistent, high-quality and confidential administrative support for executive leadership, and partner closely with the Facilities and Events teams on meeting logistics, workplace readiness and executive functions. The ideal candidate is a polished, discreet and results-oriented leader who thrives in a fast-paced financial services environment and is passionate about helping others succeed.
Key responsibilities
Team leadership and talent development
• Lead, coach and develop a team of 6–8 Executive Assistants supporting executives across the organization, fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, discretion and service excellence.
• Manage the full employee lifecycle for direct reports including recruiting, resume review, interviewing and hiring, onboarding, training, goal setting, performance reviews, succession planning and offboarding, in partnership with HR and Facilities Leadership team.
• Hold regular team meetings and 1:1 coaching sessions to share company information, clarify expectations, review performance and support each Executive Assistant’s professional goals.
• Recognize and reward strong performance, address performance gaps promptly and constructively, and resolve interpersonal issues within the team.
• Promote cross-training and knowledge sharing so the team can provide seamless backup coverage across executives and business areas.
• Identify training needs and coordinate development opportunities (research, booking, confirmations) to build skills in technology, business knowledge and executive support best practices.
Executive assistant support (as needed)
• Provide senior-level, highly confidential administrative and operational support to an assigned senior executive and, as needed, their direct reports.
• Proactively manage a complex and frequently changing calendar; schedule meetings, send invitations, book rooms and arrange technology, materials and catering to ensure smooth, well-prepared meetings.
• Manage the executive’s inbox and sensitive communications; draft, edit and distribute correspondence, presentations, reports and other materials with a high degree of accuracy and professionalism.
• Coordinate domestic and international travel, including flights, hotels, ground transportation and detailed itineraries, and prepare and reconcile expense reports in a timely manner.
• Process invoices and track departmental expenses in line with Cboe policies, vendor agreements and budget guidelines.
• Prepare briefing materials, track action items and follow up on deliverables to keep the executive’s priorities on schedule.
• Track and distribute recognition awards and other team communications on behalf of the executive, as applicable.
• Serve as a trusted liaison between the executive and internal and external stakeholders, exercising sound judgment and discretion at all times.
Executive support oversight and service standards
• Set priorities, balance workload and reassign coverage across the Executive Assistant team for PTO, transitions, peak demand or changing business needs.
• Ensure all vacation and absence scheduling is documented, follows guidelines, accounts for critical business needs and is managed consistently across the team.
• Establish, document and maintain consistent standards, best practices and SOPs for executive support, including calendaring, travel, expenses, filing and communications.
• Monitor the quality, responsiveness and consistency of service delivered to executive leadership; gather feedback from executives and act on opportunities to improve.
• Serve as the escalation point for complex scheduling, travel, logistical or service issues affecting executive leaders, and resolve them quickly and professionally.
Events, meetings and workplace coordination
• Partner with the Events team to plan and execute logistics for executive meetings, offsites, and leadership events, including room setups, AV and technology needs, and catering.
• Act as the primary liaison between the Executive Assistant team and the Events and Facilities teams so that requirements are communicated clearly and delivered on time.
• Anticipate and troubleshoot logistical needs for recurring leadership meetings, including board meetings and leadership team meetings.
• Partner with Facilities on executive-area workplace matters, including office moves, space planning, new hires and departures, furniture and equipment needs, while minimizing disruption to the business.
• Lead the planning, coordination and implementation of department events as assigned.
Operations, budget and vendor management
• Manage relationships with related vendors (e.g., catering, office services, travel) to ensure quality service, compliance with agreements and value for money.
• Develop and maintain organized filing systems so that business documents, reports and forms, paper or electronic, are accurate, complete and readily available.
Process improvement, reporting and change management
• Develop and maintain administrative processes, tools and shared resources (calendaring standards, travel and expense procedures, templates, SharePoint sites) that improve efficiency across the team.
• Identify opportunities to streamline administrative operations, reduce redundancy and adopt new technology, including AI-enabled productivity tools, where appropriate.
• Gather and analyze data to produce regular and ad hoc reports and dashboards on team workload, service levels and spend, and provide insights and recommendations to leadership.
• Lead or support change management activities for administrative initiatives, including readiness assessments, stakeholder communication, execution and sustainment.
• Stay current on industry trends and best practices in executive support and incorporate them into team operations.
Risk, compliance and confidentiality
• Handle highly confidential and sensitive information with absolute discretion in line with Cboe policies and regulatory requirements.
• Ensure the team adheres to company policies, procedures and control standards, including information security, records management and expense policies.
• Exercise sound, risk-informed judgment to identify, diagnose and resolve problems, escalating issues appropriately.
Qualifications
Required
• Bachelor’s degree or equivalent combination of education and experience.
• 12+ years of experience in executive administration, office management or administrative operations, including at least 10 years supporting senior executives (C-suite or SVP level).
• 10+ years of experience directly managing, coaching and developing administrative staff or Executive Assistants.
• 8 -10+ years of experience in the financial services industry.
• Proven ability to manage complex calendars, travel, expenses and highly confidential communications for senior leaders.
• Excellent project management skills with proven track record navigating cross functional projects, events, and teams to deliver winning outcomes and optimized solutions in the workplace.
• Strong organizational, prioritization and problem-solving skills; comfortable managing competing demands under time pressure.
• Excellent written and verbal communication skills with a polished, professional demeanor.
• High degree of discretion, integrity and judgment in handling confidential and sensitive information.
• Advanced proficiency with Microsoft 365 (Outlook, Teams, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, SharePoint) and virtual meeting tools (Teams, Zoom, Webex).
• Experience using AI tools (e.g., Claude, Microsoft Copilot) to improve productivity.
Preferred
• 15+ years of experience in financial services, an exchange or another highly regulated environment.
• 15+ years of experience coordinating with events, facilities, catering or office services vendors.
• Experience managing budgets, vendor relationships and administrative programs across multiple global teams or locations.
• Familiarity with Concur, Workday and similar enterprise tools.
• Demonstrated expertise leveraging AI tools (e.g., Claude, Microsoft Copilot) to improve executive assistant role productivity.
• Professional certification such as Certified Administrative Professional (CAP) or similar.
• Professional certification in project management.
Core competencies
• People leadership: Builds an engaged, accountable team; coaches for growth and manages performance fairly and consistently.
• Executive presence: Represents executives and Cboe with poise, credibility and sound judgment.
• Service orientation: Anticipates needs and delivers a consistent, high-quality experience for executives and stakeholders.
• Collaboration and influence: Builds strong relationships across Facilities, Events, HR, Finance and business teams to get things done.
• Analytical and data-driven: Uses data and feedback to make decisions, measure service and drive continuous improvement.

We are seeking a strategic, hands-on, and delivery-focused product leader to serve as Senior Product Manager, Executive Benefits . You will be the single accountable product leader for the digital capabilities behind Guardian's Executive Benefits business: how employers, benefit administrators, brokers, and employees enroll in, are billed for, and manage Executive Benefits Disability and Life coverage.
Executive Benefits is a priority growth market in FPRS' Journey-to-30 strategy. Our objective is clear: make Executive Benefits as easy to buy, enroll in, and administer as Group coverage. That means one place for employers to view and pay every bill, re-enrollment that runs itself, and a single enrollment experience across Life and Disability.
The vision for Executive Benefits is set by the business. In this role, you will translate that vision into a product roadmap and requirements and lead the work from discovery through launch and adoption. This role reports into the Head of Purchase & Underwriting Modernization (FPRS). You will partner closely with Executive Benefits business leaders, Digital & Technology, Operations, Underwriting, Distribution, and our Group Benefits colleagues.
A successful candidate will turn strategy into products that ship, get adopted, and deliver measurable results. You will make clear trade-offs when demand exceeds capacity, and you will hold a high bar on both what we build and how well the business is ready to use it.
What you will do
Your work will span across the following areas:
Roadmap and prioritization
• Translate the Executive Benefits business vision and strategy into the product roadmap: a committed 90-day PI roadmap with planned intent six to nine months out
• Translate value stream OKRs into 90-day product OKRs, and track outcomes (not output) on a product performance dashboard
• Partner with Executive Benefits business leaders, who own the vision, to establish the value of each capability and prioritize scope across multiple Epics
Requirements and delivery
• Write and own the Product Requirements Document (PRD); break Epics into Capabilities and Features that each fit in one PI. You are accountable for every Feature, functional or technical
• Lead Feature refinement so work meets the Definition of Ready before PI Planning, and manage dependencies across teams, value streams, and shared Group platforms
• Co-lead the product with your Digital & Technology counterpart, and lead and coach the Product Owner(s) on Executive Benefits teams
Customer experience and process design
• Drive customer journeys, personas, and prototypes with the Customer Advocacy and UX Centers of Excellence, and the product-level business process architecture
• Define data input and output requirements across employer, broker, and participant journeys
• Simplify end-to-end processes through AI and automation, working with Data and AI partners to meet Guardian's standards
Go-to-market and adoption
• Ensure Operations, Distribution, Marketing, and Compliance are ready on launch day
• Drive field and broker adoption, define adoption measures, and feed results back into the roadmap
• Give senior leaders clear, candid updates on progress, risks, and outcomes
You are
• A product leader who owns outcomes end to end, from problem statement to adoption
• Execution-minded, with a strong preference for delivery over theory
• Comfortable making and holding difficult trade-offs with senior stakeholders, using evidence rather than opinion
• Able to play high and low: shape strategy with executives, then work through acceptance criteria with a delivery team
• A clear, concise communicator with executive, field, and technical audiences
• A daily AI user who looks for ways to work faster and simplify how the business runs
You have
• Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience
• 8+ years of experience in product management or a closely related field, taking products from concept through launch and adoption
• Experience in employee benefits (executive, worksite, voluntary, multi-life disability, or group), ideally across enrollment, billing, case installation, or benefits administration
• Proven ownership of a PRD, product OKRs, and a roadmap in a scaled agile (SAFe/PI) environment, using tools such as SPM and Jira
• Experience with employer and benefit-administrator integrations, such as single sign-on, census and eligibility file exchange, and third-party enrollment platforms
• Strong business judgment: you connect capabilities to sales, persistency, expense, and customer experience outcomes
• Practical fluency with Microsoft 365 Copilot or similar AI tools in product work (drafting PRDs, breaking down Features, synthesizing research)
• Insurance or regulated financial services experience preferred; SAFe POPM or similar certification a plus
You will
• Drive one of FPRS' priority growth markets as its single accountable technology product leader
• Shape how employers, brokers, and employees experience Guardian across Executive Benefits and Group
• Work closely with senior business, technology, and distribution leaders
• Grow as a product leader in Guardian's business and technology operating model
Location
This role is hybrid with 3 days per week in a Guardian Hub (Hudson Yards, Boston, Bethlehem, Pittsfield, Holmdel).

American International Group, Inc. (AIG) is a leading global insurance organization. AIG member companies provide a wide range of property casualty insurance in approximately 70 countries and jurisdictions. These diverse offerings include products and services that help businesses and individuals protect their assets and manage risks.
At AIG, we are reimagining the way we help customers to manage risk. Join us as an Actuarial Data and & Tools - Lead Business Analyst to play your part in that transformation. It’s an opportunity to grow your skills and experience as a valued member of the team.
Make Your Mark:
AIG is a leading provider of insurance products and services – focused on helping to manage risk for commercial and personal customers. We offer a broad range of products through a diversified, multi-channel distribution network, including one of the world’s most far-reaching property casualty networks. The Data Office supports the overall General Insurance product by managing Data, Data Governance, and the presentation of the data (Business Intelligence Delivery).
How you will create an impact:
AIG is looking for a driven individual to assume a critical role within the Data Office. This role will work directly with the Actuarial and Data teams to ensure a clear understanding of data and analytics needs and priorities. In addition, the individual will hold Global Data Warehouse Product Ownership responsibilities, ensuring execution aligns with the highest business priorities and Data Office strategy, and that sunset opportunities are realized.
About the Role
The Actuarial Data & Tools - Lead Business Analyst role sits within the Global Data Office at the intersection of business strategy, data, and analytics, and works closely with Commercial Lines Actuarial Groups. The ideal candidate will have a strong understanding of actuarial concepts (reserving, pricing, and risk assessment), proven data and analytics capabilities, excellent communication skills, and experience as an Agile Product Owner. In this role, you will translate complex actuarial business requirements into actionable data engineering specifications by collaborating directly with data development teams. As a trusted business partner and product owner within the Global Data Warehouse, this role will help shape how AIG uses data to make better decisions, simplify its analytics landscape, and focus investments where they matter most .
Responsibilities
Business Requirements: Lead deep, structured requirement sessions with senior actuaries to understand workflows, data nuances, and reporting needs, creating detailed functional specifications.
• Stakeholder Management: Facilitate alignment across actuaries and Data Office teams on project priorities, project timelines, and management of the deliverables.
• Product Owner for Data Platform & Tool Development: Develop roadmaps for actuarial data and tool development requirements and partner with data engineers to build and deploy them in timely manner.
• Agile Development Leadership & Product Backlog Management
• Lead Agile Ceremonies: Act as the Business Analyst Lead within an agile team, facilitating user story refinement, sprint planning, and daily scrums.
• Backlog Grooming: Translate actuarial requirements (reserving, pricing, modeling) into actionable user stories, epics, and acceptance criteria for developers.
• Data Governance & Quality: Ensure compliance with data standards and maintain rigorous documentation for data lineage, testing, and production changes.
What you'll need to succeed
• Experience: 7+ years of experience in business analysis, actuarial tool design within the insurance/financial industry.
• Education: Bachelor’s degree in actuarial science, Computer Science, Data Analytics, Mathematics, or related field.
• Actuarial Knowledge: Strong understanding of Commercial Insurance actuarial concepts (e.g., reserving methods, pricing tools)
• Data Proficiency: Experience with data environments, ETL and visualization tools
• Leadership: Demonstrated experience leading Agile teams and managing product backlogs.
• Soft Skills: Excellent communication skills, with the ability to translate technical concepts to non-technical stakeholders.
• Preferred Qualifications: Actuarial Credentials, actuarial exams, or deep understanding of actuarial reserving/pricing concepts.
Ready to make a bigger impact? We look forward to reviewing your application.
Veterans are encouraged to apply.

The architect team has four domains that together make the platform work for customers: Platform Advantage, Emerging Tech & UI Innovation, Data & AI Excellence, and Governance & Trust. This role sits in Governance & Trust, which covers identity, security, and audit.
Agents now take actions, call tools, and work with other agents, often across systems Salesforce doesn’t own. Each step prompts the same questions from a customer’s security and risk leaders: who is this agent acting as, what can it touch, who approved it, and how do we stop it?
You answer those questions with architecture, not assurances. When an AI program reaches the security review, the risk committee, or the Chief Information Security Officer, you show how identity, data access, agent authority, and audit work, and what it takes to prove it.
You start from the customer’s risk and business problem, not a product pitch. You stay engaged until the controls are in place, because trust is what lets AI scale.

• Define agent guardrails, runtime control, observability, and audit using the Einstein Trust Layer, deterministic controls, human-in-the-loop, governance of external agents, event monitoring, agent session tracing, and security information and event management (SIEM) integration
• Lead AI governance and risk work, including risk tiering, approval gates, and regulatory readiness, while aligning C-suite stakeholders and working with pre-sale and post-sale teams to resolve platform-fit questions for customers

• 5+ years in enterprise or solutions architecture, with direct experience influencing senior technical and business stakeholders and staying engaged through delivery, including recovering stalled work

• B.S., M.S. or PhD in Computer Science, Software Engineering or MIS

• Strong understanding of statistical modeling, LLMs, machine learning, and quantitative model assessment techniques.
• Demonstrated ability to critically evaluate model methodologies, assumptions, data, performance measures, limitations, and validation approaches.
• Strong analytical and critical-thinking skills, including the ability to determine whether quantitative evidence supports model development, validation, and risk-management conclusions.

• Knowledge of AI/ML methods such as regression, classification, clustering, tree-based methods, gradient boosting, neural networks, natural language processing, and other advanced analytical techniques.
• Knowledge of model risk management frameworks and regulatory expectations applicable to financial institutions, including model development, independent validation, implementation, ongoing monitoring, change management, and model governance.

Company Description
Etsy is the global marketplace for unique and creative goods. We build, power, and evolve the tools and technologies that connect millions of entrepreneurs with millions of buyers around the world. As an Etsy employee, you will tackle unique, meaningful, and large-scale problems alongside passionate coworkers, all the while making a rewarding impact and Keeping Commerce Human.
We believe exceptional companies are built by exceptional teams, and we're intentional about it. That means hiring great people, setting them up for success from day one, and giving them real reasons to grow their careers here. We invest in development that goes beyond promotions, and we foster the trust and relationships that help people do their best work together.
What’s the role?
The Investigator role performs core enforcement reviews, conducting deep-dive fraud and/or account integrity investigations, and analyzing fraud and security trends using data tools and internal systems. Key responsibilities include doing queue based account reviews, providing feedback to improve machine learning models, designing and implementing new detection and enforcement controls, leading designing and implementing tooling and process enhancements, and assessing fraud risk for new products. This role goes deep in the details, both with task based queue work and large, comprehensive investigations.
This is a full-time position reporting to the Director, Fraud.
What’s this team like at Etsy?
The Integrity, Risk, and Regulatory Operations teams identify, investigate, and mitigate financial crimes, regulatory risks, and fraud patterns, with particular attention to buyer and seller behaviors that can span accounts, payments, and collusive abuse. The team balances sharp investigative thinking with long-term systems building, using operational insight to shape scalable defenses and improve how we detect and respond to emerging risk.
What does the day-to-day look like?
• Conduct deep-dive investigations into complex fraud or account security cases and chargeback patterns.
• Manage queue-based account reviews as needed.
• Use SQL and Looker to identify emerging trends and provide actionable insights.
• Support ML model development by providing subject matter expertise and operational feedback.
• Collaborate on new product launches to assess fraud risks and design controls.
• Contribute to building and delivering training and documentation to enable and upskill the broader operations team.
• Of course, this is just a sample of the kinds of work this role will require! You should assume that your role will encompass other tasks, too, and that your job duties and responsibilities may change from time to time at Etsy's discretion, or otherwise applicable with local law.
Qualities that will help you thrive in this role are:
• 3+ years of experience in fraud prevention, account security, or risk management, ideally within e-commerce or marketplaces.
• Proficiency in SQL and data visualization tools such as Looker or Tableau to extract actionable insights.
• Strong analytical and critical thinking skills to conduct deep-dive investigations into complex cases.
• Experience leading operational excellence initiatives such as QA, training, knowledge management, workflow design, or business process improvement.
• A collaborative mindset and a strong sense of ownership for both the quality of your own work and the effectiveness of the broader organization.
Compensation & Benefits
In addition to salary, you'll be eligible for an equity package, an annual performance bonus, and our competitive benefits that support you and your family. Base salary is determined by your location, skills, and experience.

Introduction to The Team:
The Product Team creates high-quality end-to-end experiences for travelers, partners, and Expedia Group. Search and Recommendations are the front door to every trip travelers plan on Expedia, Hotels.com, and Vrbo: from the ranked results on a search results page to the recommendation modules that suggest the next property, destination, or add-on. The ranking and relevance decisions made across these surfaces in a fraction of a second shape whether a traveler finds the right option, and whether that moment converts into a booking. As Search & Recs grows in scale and complexity across brands, our ability to measure relevance and engagement quality, diagnose regressions, and benchmark against the competition becomes essential to protecting and growing that value.
The Search & Recs Quality team defines how Expedia Group measures and improves the health of search ranking and recommendation surfaces. We build the metrics, evaluation tooling, and operating cadences that tell Search, Recs, ML, and Engineering teams whether ranking and recommendations are working for travelers, for suppliers, and for the business and where to focus the next improvement.
In this role, you will own product quality and relevance measurement across all Search and Recommendations surfaces, partnering closely with Ranking and Personalization ML Science, ML Engineering, and Search Engineering to turn ambiguous relevance and engagement questions into clear, defensible metrics and roadmap decisions. Your work will directly influence how travelers experience search results and recommendations across brands, and how confidently the organization can ship ranking and personalization changes.

• Own the product vision and roadmap for search and recommendations quality measurement, mapping target outcomes and KPIs (e.g., relevance, ranking quality, recommendation engagement, search-to-booking success) to delivery milestones
• Partner with ML Science and ML Engineering to define and evaluate ranking and recommendation model quality including offline metrics (e.g., NDCG@10) and online proxies (e.g., Average Booking Position, recommendation click-through and conversion) and to facilitate technical tradeoff decisions on model changes
• Own and scale evaluation system for search relevance: a curated query corpus, human relevance annotation, and LLM-as-judge scoring, reported through our larger Search Health program and extend these methods to evaluate recommendation surfaces (e.g., destination recs, cross-sell, rebooking recommendations)
• Define and own product metrics for search relevance and recommendation quality, running regular metric reviews and holding the roadmap accountable to measurable outcomes across both surfaces
• Lead competitive relevance and recommendation benchmarking against key players in the marketplace, translating findings into a prioritized set of product, ranking, and personalization investments
• Coordinate experimentation and win-loss analysis on ranking, relevance, and recommendation changes, recommending strategies to optimize quality across brands
• Coach and influence PMs and stakeholders across the broader Search & Recs organization on relevance and recommendation quality measurement best practices
Minimum Requirements:
• Bachelor's degree in a technical, quantitative, or related field, or equivalent practical experience; 8+ years of product management experience (6+ years with a Master's degree)
• Experience owning product metrics, experimentation, or evaluation frameworks for a ranking, recommendations, personalization, or search system
• Strong technical depth and experience partnering directly with ML Science/ML Engineering teams on model evaluation and tradeoffs
• Demonstrated ability to independently design product experiments, interpret ranking, relevance, or recommendation engagement data, and translate findings into a defensible roadmap
• Track record of driving milestone and release planning for complex, cross-functional initiatives, including proactive risk mitigation
• Strong written and verbal communication skills, including experience presenting to and influencing senior stakeholders
Preferred Qualifications:
• Experience with search ranking and/or recommendation systems (e.g., learning-to-rank models, collaborative filtering, NDCG, engagement and conversion metrics)
• Familiarity with LLM-as-judge or other AI-assisted relevance and recommendation evaluation methods
• Experience in a marketplace or travel/e-commerce search and recommendations context, balancing traveler relevance with supplier and commercial considerations
• Experience running or contributing to competitive benchmarking programs across search and/or recommendation surfaces

Job Description:
About the Team:
Dow Jones is a global provider of news and business information, delivering content to consumers and organizations around the world across multiple formats, including print, digital, mobile, and live events. Dow Jones has produced unrivaled quality content for more than 130 years and today has one of the world’s largest news-gathering operations globally. It is home to leading publications and products including the flagship Wall Street Journal, Barron’s, MarketWatch, Mansion Global, Financial News, Investor’s Business Daily, Factiva, Dow Jones Risk & Compliance, Dow Jones Newswires, OPIS, and Chemical Market Analytics. Dow Jones is a division of News Corp (Nasdaq: NWS, NWSA; ASX: NWS, NWSLV).
The Customer Insights team supports Dow Jones' strategic goals by providing a clear, actionable understanding of our consumer markets, subscribers, brand positioning, and product offerings through primary market and user research. We partner closely with consumer marketing, brand, strategy, product, and newsroom partners across our consumer media portfolio to convert consumer feedback, synthetic data, and quantitative analytics into high-impact business decisions.
About the Role :
We are seeking a Senior Manager, Customer Insights to serve as a senior strategic research lead within our Consumer Organization.
In this role, you will lead high-impact quantitative and qualitative research initiatives that directly inform strategic decision-making across Consumer Marketing, Brand, and Ventures for our media properties (including WSJ, Barron's, MarketWatch, and IBD). As a senior individual contributor, you will not manage direct reports, but you will play a critical strategic leadership role across the Consumer org. You will be responsible for end-to-end execution of complex B2C research projects, overseeing agency and research vendor partnerships, driving modern AI-enabled research workflows, and building collaborative relationships with senior cross-functional stakeholders.
The Senior Manager, Customer Insights, will report to the VP, Customer Insights.
You Will:
• Design, execute, and synthesize high-impact primary quantitative and qualitative research projects (e.g., brand health, concept testing, pricing/packaging, audience positioning, message/creative testing, and exploratory market studies) to support Consumer Marketing, Brand, and Ventures goals.
• Champion modern consumer research methodologies by leveraging cutting-edge GenAI tools, AI agentic systems, AI-powered qualitative-at-scale platforms, and synthetic data models/AI twins to accelerate consumer insights generation and efficiency.
• Serve as a trusted advisor to senior partners across Consumer Marketing, Brand, Subscription Strategy, and Business Development/Ventures. Translate ambiguous consumer business questions into structured research objectives and deliver actionable, strategic insights.
• Oversee research agency relationships and third-party vendors (including panel providers and emerging AI research platforms) from briefing and methodology selection through procurement, fieldwork execution, and final deliverables.
• Manage and evolve core tracking programs and strategic research initiatives.
• Distill complex quantitative datasets, consumer feedback, and AI-enabled research outputs into concise, executive-ready presentations that influence subscriber growth, engagement, and retention strategies.
• Partner effectively across the broader Customer Insights team, Data Science/Analytics, UX/Product, and Marketing teams to ensure alignment and maximize the business impact of research findings.
You Have:
• 10+ years of primary qualitative and quantitative consumer market research experience, ideally within digital media, news/publishing, direct-to-consumer (DTC) subscription models, or strategic research agencies.
• Deep experience executing a wide array of primary research methods (surveys, focus groups, IDIs, diaries, online communities) and statistical analysis techniques (correlation, regression, conjoint, max diff, statistical significance)
• Proficient in standard survey, moderation and data analysis platforms (e.g., Qualtrics, SPSS, Discuss.io, Excel, data visualization dashboards).
• Hands-on experience using generative AI platforms and large language models (e.g., NotebookLM, Gemini, Claude, ChatGPT) for desk research, data synthesis, research brief and questionnaire drafting, and qualitative coding.
• Familiarity with AI agentic tools, conversational AI interview platforms, AI-assisted qual-at-scale, or synthetic audience models/AI twins.
• Proven experience sourcing, managing, and partnering with research vendors, consumer sample providers, and research platforms and applications.
• Demonstrated ability to build strong relationships across a matrixed consumer organization, influence senior leaders, and drive research agendas without direct managerial authority.
• Exceptional storytelling, written presentation, and narrative-building skills—ability to convert raw consumer data into clear strategic recommendations.
• Experience managing multiple concurrent projects and deadlines
• Proficiency with Google Suite
• Bachelor’s degree in Social Sciences, Business, Marketing, Data Analytics, or a related field (advanced degree highly preferred).

Job Description:
Why This Role
Reputation Radar is sold, serviced and marketed by Dow Jones teams in New York, while product, engineering, data science and Go-to-Market (GTM) strategy sit with Storyful in Dublin. Today one person in Dublin covers both sides. That works for strategy, messaging, pricing and the Early Access Program, which all sit close to product. It does not work for the parts of GTM that depend on being in the room with sellers, customer success and Dow Jones marketing every day.
Three things we cannot do today, and what this role unlocks:
1. Sales and CES enablement inside Dow Jones: Reps and Customer Success (CS) Managers need someone they can grab before a call, sit with after a demo, and hand objections to the same day. This role gives Dow Jones sales and CS a named Rep Radar person in New York, and gives us a live read on sales sentiment to content.
2. Campaigns through Dow Jones channels: Dow Jones B2B marketing, events and SDR teams run their own queues and priorities. Rep Radar competes for attention from Dublin by email. The role works those queues in person, turns GTM priorities into campaigns that ship through Dow Jones channels, creating the content, copy and assets as well as reports what they deliver.
3. A structured competitive and customer insight loop: We track Signal AI, Meltwater, Cision, Brandwatch and Blackbird.AI ad hoc, and we run the risk of hearing about lost deals too late. This role owns competitive tracking, win/loss reporting, and the feedback path from sellers and customers back to product and messaging, so decisions on positioning and roadmap are made on evidence rather than anecdote.
This position delivers complementary capacity enabling the Senior Product Marketing Manager to retain full ownership of launch strategy, while providing the local execution support required.
About the Role
Reputation Radar is a decision-grade reputation intelligence platform developed by Storyful and Dow Jones. Combining Factiva's licensed news archive with Storyful's human-verified social intelligence, it helps corporate affairs and communications leaders in financial services see and
act on reputational risk.
An invite-only Early Access Program is underway and general availability is scheduled for January 2027. Product, engineering and data science are led by Storyful in Dublin, alongside the Senior Product Marketing Manager who owns GTM strategy and the launch. Sales, customer success, revenue
operations and B2B marketing are run by Dow Jones in New York.
This role is Reputation Radar's presence inside the Dow Jones commercial organization. You will sit with the sellers, customer success managers and marketers who take Reputation Radar to market, make them effective, and bring what they learn back to the product and GTM team in Dublin.
You will work in our Midtown Manhattan office 3 days a week.

Sales and customer success enablement
• Be the day-to-day Reputation Radar contact for Dow Jones sales and Customer Success in New York
• Support the build and maintenance of the enablement kit: pitch decks, demo scripts, ICP guides, battle cards and collateral sheets, working from the positioning and messaging set by the Senior PMM
• Run ongoing enablement cadence, and track which materials get used and which do not
• Join prospect and customer calls and feed what you hear into messaging, enablement and the product feedback loop
Campaigns through Dow Jones channels
• Work directly with Dow Jones B2B marketing, events and SDR teams to turn Radar GTM priorities into campaigns that ship through Dow Jones channels and audiences
• Own the campaign calendar for Reputation Radar within Dow Jones marketing, including nurture email, webinars, events and paid or partner activity
• Coordinate campaign activation in addition to owning collateral production, supporting bandwidth across Dow Jones and Storyful teams
• Produce and version the collateral those campaigns need: web pages, executive summaries, one-pagers and event materials, on brand and on message
• Report campaign performance and pipeline contribution back to the Senior PMM and Dow Jones marketing leads, with recommendations on what to scale and what to stop
Competitive and customer insight
• Own competitive tracking across named competitors, and publish a regular competitive brief for product, sales and marketing
• Run the win/loss program: liaise with sellers and analyze reports to understand our competitive position
• Work with the Senior PMM to turn the findings into sales enablement updates, messaging and roadmap input
• Support the structured feedback path from Dow Jones sales, CS and customers back to the Storyful product team, so market signal reaches roadmap and positioning decisions in a usable form

We are:
A forward-thinking services company at the forefront of AI-native innovation. We partner with enterprise clients to reinvent the business processes that run their operations — finance, supply chain, customer operations, HR and industry-specific processes — by redesigning how the work is done and wiring intelligent agents into the systems the client already owns. Our people embed deeply with customers, moving projects beyond experimentation into operational reality where the result shows up in a measured business metric.
You are:
This is not a consulting role. It is not a project delivery role. It is not a research position. A Forward Deployed AI Engineer is a production engineer who works embedded inside a client's enterprise, shoulder to shoulder with their teams, to make complex AI platforms work in real, messy organizational environments. You own outcomes: time-to-value, adoption, reliability, and scalability. Not delivery milestones. Outcomes.
The market is beginning to understand what leading technology companies have demonstrated: AI products fail not because the models are weak but because deployment is broken. The gap between a successful AI pilot and an AI capability that scales is bridged by engineers who can translate platform capability into measurable business value inside a real enterprise environment. That is this role.
You are a techno-functional engineer with a minimum of five years of software engineering experience who can hold two things at once: how a business process actually works, and how to build the agents and integrations that change it. You thrive in ambiguity, you would rather show a working version than write a specification, and you are comfortable being in front of the client as well as building.
The Work:
Forward Deployed AI Engineers form the execution spine of our Reinvention Deployment Engineering pods. We are building the largest FDE capability in the services industry. The engineers who join at this stage will define what the role looks like at scale and will have access to the hardest enterprise AI problems in the market across every industry.
You will embed directly with clients as both engineer and advisor, working in a small team to take a bounded slice of a real operational process from redesign, through proof on the client's own historical data, into production on the client's own systems. The systems you work with are rarely new: you will be wiring agents into an existing estate of enterprise platforms, ISV products and installed automation, and the integration is usually harder than the build.
Key Responsibilities:
• Lead enterprise AI platform deployments across complex multi-stakeholder client environments - Anthropic, OpenAI, Microsoft, Google, Salesforce, SAP, or Palantir - owning the full program from architecture through adoption
• Own program-level delivery outcomes: time-to-value, reliability, adoption velocity, and scalability across multiple concurrent workstreams, with commercial metrics attached
• Lead rapid experimentation at pace: drive ambiguous business problems to working production systems in days or weeks across complex enterprise environments
• Architect and govern enterprise AI solutions across the full technology stack: identity, data, security, governance, platform layer, and multi-system workflow integration at programme scale
• Shape AI reinvention strategy for client CTO, CFO, and CISO: build value architecture, ROI backlogs, use case prioritisation frameworks, and multi-year AI adoption roadmaps
• Define and publish reusable reinvention blueprints, patterns, and accelerators that scale across multiple client engagements and grow the FDE practice
• Lead architecture design sessions, executive workshops, and code-with sessions with client engineering and C-suite leadership teams
• Codify delivery learnings, failure patterns, and engineering standards that shape the FDE practice and enable the next generation of forward deployed engineers
How this role differs from a general AI engineering role:
We are not hiring people to build models or chatbots. We are hiring people who can take an existing operational process — one that runs on an ERP, a handful of ISV platforms and an installed base of RPA — and make it measurably faster, cheaper or more accurate, then prove it with numbers. That requires functional understanding of the process alongside engineering depth.
Candidates with strong agentic engineering skills but no exposure to a real business process, and candidates with deep process knowledge but no ability to build, are not the right fit for this role.
• Process redesign: map the process as it is actually run rather than as it is documented, collapse steps and handoffs, and design where a human decides and where an agent may act.
• Agent architecture and engineering: design and build enterprise-ready agents covering retrieval, orchestration, policy-based routing, tool invocation, evaluation harnesses and lifecycle observability.
• Proof and measurement: build the harness that replays historical transactions, measure the before-and-after against the agreed baseline, and be straight about what the number does and does not prove.
• Integration: build and test the named integrations into systems of record, ISV platforms, document and data services, and the existing automation estate.
• Client engagement: run design workshops, build-with sessions and demonstrations, working directly with process owners and their teams.
• Leave something behind: harvest reusable connectors, evaluation sets and process patterns, so the next engagement starts further ahead than this one did.
Travel may be required for this role. The amount of travel will vary from 25% to 75% depending on business need and client requirements.
Here's What You Need:
• Minimum of 5 years of engineering experience with cloud-native systems, including APIs, microservices, containerization, and serverless architectures (Hands-on integration experience with enterprise platforms such as ERP, CRM, ITSM, procurement or core industry systems is preferred) .
• Minimum of 5 years of experience leading software engineering teams, including delivery oversight, resource allocation, and professional development of direct reports
• Minimum of 1 year of experience designing and deploying agentic solutions (agents, orchestration, context engineering, RAG, workflows) in production environments
• Minimum of 2 years of experience with AI platforms (OpenAI, Claude, Vertex AI, or open-source models), including building abstraction layers for multi-provider pipelines
• Minimum of 2 years of experience leading enterprise AI deployments across multi-stakeholder environments and working on a business or operational process domain (finance, supply chain, customer, HR or industry operations).
• Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering or equivalent, OR equivalent work experience (minimum 12 years). If an Associate's Degree, minimum 6 years of work experience.
Professional Skills Requirements
A minimum of two years working on a business or operational process domain, in a delivery, operations, transformation or product capacity.
Demonstrable depth in at least one of the following process domains, evidenced by having worked on how the process actually runs rather than only on the systems that support it:
• Finance operations — accounts payable and procure-to-pay (invoice capture and coding, two-way and three-way match, exception handling, duplicate and overpayment prevention, early-payment discount capture, payment runs); order-to-cash (billing, collections, cash application, deductions, revenue leakage); record-to-report (close, reconciliations, intercompany, journal review); expenses and travel; treasury operations.
• Supply chain and procurement operations — sourcing and contract operations, supplier onboarding and master data, demand and supply planning exceptions, freight and logistics audit, inventory and fulfilment exceptions.
• Customer and service operations — service desk and ticket triage, case management, claims first notice of loss and adjudication, billing disputes, customer onboarding, order management.
• HR operations — hire-to-retire, payroll exceptions, benefits and case management, employee query resolution.
• Industry operations — for example KYC and periodic refresh, AML alert triage, payments exceptions and policy servicing in financial services; prior authorization and claims in health; quality and deviation handling in life sciences; network and field operations in communications and utilities.
• Ability to establish and defend a process baseline with a client's finance or controlling function, for example – unit cost per transaction, touchless or straight-through rate, cycle time, first-pass yield, rework and exception rate, and leakage prevented.
• Experience measuring a before-and-after delta on a real process and explaining it to a business audience without overstating it.
Bonus points if you have
• Process mining or process modelling tooling — Celonis, SAP Signavio, ARIS, UiPath Process Mining, Microsoft Power Automate process mining or equivalent.
• Working with automation tools like — UiPath, Blue Prism, Automation Anywhere, Power Automate, SAP Build Process Automation.

We Are
Accenture Security helps organizations prepare, protect, detect, respond, and recover along with all points of the security lifecycle. Cybersecurity challenges are different for every business in every industry. Leveraging our global resources and advanced technologies, we create integrated, turnkey solutions tailored to our client's needs across their entire value chain. Whether we’re defending against known cyberattacks, detecting and responding to the unknown, or running an entire security operations center, we will help companies build cyber resilience to grow with confidence. Our team of the security sector’s brightest people uses the coolest tech to out-hack the hackers and help clients build resilience from within. We blend risk strategy, digital identity, cyber defense, application security, and managed service solutions to rethink the entire security lifecycle.
Do you have the deep functional and technical experience to help implement security solutions that align with our clients’ business objectives? Do you have the expertise to design and deliver solutions for establishing system user's credentials, and processes for applying those credentials to access enterprise systems and applications?
You Are
The Cybersecurity Security Compliance Consultant will independently execute assigned compliance assessment and documentation activities across CMMC, FedRAMP, and NIST-based programs — working within structured delivery frameworks under the guidance of Senior Consultants and Managers. The Consultant takes ownership of specific assessment tasks and documentation deliverables, bringing analytical rigor, detail orientation, and clear written communication to every work product.
This role is a key execution contributor on security compliance engagements. The Consultant performs control assessments, develops compliance documentation, supports evidence gathering and analysis, maintains compliance trackers, and participates directly in client working sessions. Engagements will span CMMC Level 1 and Level 2 readiness support, FedRAMP authorization package development, NIST SP 800-53 and NIST SP 800-171 assessments, and A&A support across Products industry and federal program clients.
The Consultant is expected to develop expertise in CMMC, FedRAMP, and NIST frameworks through direct program experience and structured mentorship, with a clear growth path toward greater workstream ownership at the Senior Consultant level.
Travel may be required for this role. The amount of travel will vary from 0 to 100% depending on business need and client requirements.
Here’s what we need
• Minimum of 3 years of cybersecurity, compliance, or information security experience with demonstrated responsibility for producing work products such as assessments, gap analyses, compliance documentation, evidence packages, or authorization artifacts
• Minimum of 3 years direct experience in a compliance-focused domain — specifically CMMC, FedRAMP, NIST SP 800-53, or NIST SP 800-171 — OR minimum 1 year of experience in a relevant Products industry (Aerospace & Defense, Consumer Goods, Life Sciences) with demonstrated exposure to regulated compliance activities; general NIST CSF awareness alone does not satisfy this requirement
• Minimum of 3 years demonstrated ability to independently execute compliance assessment tasks — including reviewing policies and procedures, gathering and validating evidence, conducting interviews, and documenting findings with specificity against applicable standard requirements
• Minimum of 3 years working knowledge of security assessment and authorization (A&A) methodology — including the three assessment methods (examine, interview, test), evidence sufficiency criteria, finding documentation standards, and the Authorization to Operate (ATO) workflow under FISMA, FedRAMP, and NIST RMF
• Bachelor's degree or equivalent (minimum 12 years work experience; Associate's Degree + minimum 6 years work experience)
Professional Skills requirements
• Familiarity with CMMC Level 1 and Level 2 Practice requirements and the relationship between CMMC Practices and NIST SP 800-171 rev 2 requirements — including understanding of how CMMC scoping and CUI identification impact assessment boundary and practice applicability
• Proficiency with Microsoft Office tools — Excel for tracker maintenance and data analysis, PowerPoint for client deliverables and briefings, Word for documentation drafting and review
• CMMC Registered Practitioner (RP) — entry-level Cyber AB practitioner credential demonstrating formal training in CMMC advisory, OSC readiness support, and implementation guidance; preferred for candidates in client-facing compliance delivery roles; actively pursuing RP is valued if not yet obtained
• CompTIA Security+, CompTIA CySA+, or equivalent mid-level cybersecurity certification demonstrating foundational security knowledge and professional commitment
• FedRAMP-specific experience — including contribution to RAR development, SSP control narratives, continuous monitoring reporting, or Agency/JAB authorization lifecycle activities
• DoD or Defense Industrial Base (DIB) experience — including awareness of DFARS 252.204-7012, CUI handling requirements (32 CFR Part 2002), and CMMC compliance expectations for DIB contractors and their subcontractor supply chains
• Experience with GRC or compliance management platforms — ServiceNow GRC, ZenGRC, Drata, Archer, or equivalent tools used for evidence management, tracker maintenance, and assessment workflow suppor
• Proficiency with Microsoft 365 collaboration tools — SharePoint for document management, Teams for project coordination, and Planner or similar tools for task tracking
• Foundational cloud security knowledge (AWS, Azure, or Microsoft 365 environments) relevant to cloud system scoping, configuration review, and inherited control analysis in CMMC and FedRAMP contexts
• Strong documentation and analytical writing skills — demonstrated ability to produce clear, structured, client-ready compliance narratives, gap reports, and POA&M entries
• Exposure to consulting or professional services delivery environments — including experience working with defined deliverable standards, client protocols, and team hierarchies

We are looking for an experienced Research Portfolio Analyst to support the National Institute on Minority Health and Health Disparities (NIMHD) by providing scientific, analytical, programmatic, and coordination support to Federal Program Officers overseeing diverse research portfolios. This is a full-time position located in Bethesda, MD.
• Compile, clean, organize, and analyze scientific and program data from Government-approved sources; check data quality, identify limitations, and prepare authorized extracts, tables, charts, graphs, dashboards, inventories, and factual summaries.
• Participate in scientific and program meetings; document discussions, Government decisions, action items, and follow-up needs in draft summaries and briefings.
• Plan and coordinate scientific meetings, workshops, conferences, symposia, lectures, and special projects, including agendas, participant materials, logistics, presentations, and follow-up.
• Support project management and cross-divisional coordination for large or complex scientific programs; maintain documentation, communications, schedules, trackers, and action logs; track activities, milestones, deadlines, dependencies, and deliverables; and provide consolidated status updates and reminders.
• Search PubMed, Web of Science, and other scientific sources; interpret, analyze, and summarize literature, reports, and background materials in literature reviews, environmental scans, annotated references, source summaries, and scientific memoranda.
• Develop scientific and program presentations, including slides, tables, graphs, charts, abstracts, posters, handouts, and briefing materials.
• Coordinate scheduling, information requests, meeting logistics, and follow-up communications with internal and external stakeholders as authorized by the Government.
• Prepare progress, monthly status, and technical reports; portfolio summaries; spreadsheets; correspondence; and other scientific and program documentation.
• Analyze scientific programs, research portfolios, and grantee information by grant mechanism or scientific topic to identify factual trends, gaps, recurring issues, data limitations, and operational matters for Federal staff consideration.
• Assist with management and administrative analyses of procedures, policies, processes, and systems to support operational efficiency.
• Maintain Government-approved program data, inventories, databases, logs, SharePoint repositories, and other information resources.
• Ensure scientific judgments, grants stewardship, policy interpretations, funding decisions, approvals, and inherently governmental functions remain with authorized Federal personnel.

• A Master’s degree in a relevant scientific, health, behavioral, social science, public health, data science, interdisciplinary, or related field.
• Minimum of TWO (2) years of experience supporting NIH biomedical, behavioral, social, public health, data science, or other scientific research programs.
• Knowledge of NIH grants, funding mechanisms, and Federal extramural research programs.
• Experience analyzing scientific and Federal research portfolios, including grantee progress and scientific program reviews.
• Experience collecting, cleaning, organizing, analyzing, and presenting scientific or programmatic data, including dashboards, visualizations, and portfolio inventories.
• Strong technical and scientific writing and verbal communication skills, including preparing reports, summaries, executive-level briefings, agendas, and other professional documents and conveying scientific and technical information clearly using plain language when appropriate.
• Experience supporting and coordinating scientific meetings, workshops, conferences, lectures, and stakeholder events.
• Strong project management and organizational skills, including maintaining schedules, trackers, milestones, deadlines, and action items.
• Ability to work effectively with Federal staff and internal and external scientific stakeholders.
• Familiarity with minority health, health disparities, public health, biomedical, behavioral, or social science research portfolios.
• Experience conducting scientific literature research using PubMed and Web of Science and using bibliographic or reference-management software.
• Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite, Adobe Acrobat, SharePoint, and collaborative productivity tools; advanced Excel skills for data analysis, organization, visualization, and reporting; and experience developing or maintaining SharePoint sites, research databases, program trackers, or data analytics tools.
• Must be able to obtain and maintain a Federal or DoD “public trust”; candidates must receive approved adjudication prior to onboarding with Guidehouse. Candidates with an active public trust or suitability are preferred.

Senior Strategy Leader
Purplemoon, an IQVIA Business
About Purplemoon
Purplemoon, an IQVIA company, is an award-winning healthcare communications agency specializing in pharmaceutical marketing, rare diseases, and complex therapeutic categories. We partner with biopharmaceutical organizations to transform scientific innovation into meaningful brand experiences that engage healthcare professionals, patients, caregivers, and key stakeholders.
By combining deep scientific expertise, strategic insight, creativity, and data-driven decision-making, Purplemoon delivers innovative solutions across brand strategy, commercialization, product launches, patient engagement, and omnichannel communications. As part of IQVIA's global healthcare ecosystem, Purplemoon leverages industry-leading data, analytics, technology, and therapeutic expertise to help clients accelerate the adoption of life-changing therapies and improve patient outcomes worldwide.
Our culture is built on collaboration, curiosity, innovation, and a passion for making a meaningful difference in healthcare.
Position Summary
The Senior Strategy Leader is a senior leadership role responsible for leading strategic planning and brand development for an assigned portfolio of pharmaceutical, biotechnology, and healthcare clients.
This individual serves as a trusted advisor, business partner, and strategic leader, helping clients translate scientific innovation, market insights, and customer needs into impactful commercial strategies and communication programs.
Reporting to the Head of Strategy, the Senior Strategy Leader will collaborate across Account, Medical, Creative, Analytics, and Consulting teams to develop innovative solutions that drive brand growth, customer engagement, and business success.
Key Responsibilities
Strategic Leadership
• Develop brand positioning, value propositions, messaging frameworks, and integrated communications strategies across the product lifecycle.
• Translate market research, clinical data, customer insights, competitive intelligence, and healthcare trends into actionable business recommendations.
• Lead strategic planning for pre-launch, launch, and post-launch brands.
• Develop customer-centric strategies for healthcare professionals (HCPs), patients, caregivers, payers, and other key stakeholders.
• Partner with cross-functional teams to ensure strategic alignment and execution excellence.
Client Leadership
• Serve as a trusted strategic advisor to senior client stakeholders.
• Design and facilitate workshops, advisory boards, strategic planning sessions, and executive presentations.
• Build and strengthen long-term client partnerships.
• Provide thought leadership on industry trends, commercialization strategies, customer engagement, and market evolution.
• Identify opportunities to expand client engagements and deliver additional value.
Team & Agency Leadership
• Collaborate closely with Account, Creative, Medical, Analytics, and Consulting teams.
• Establish strategic planning standards, frameworks, and best practices.
• Mentor and develop Strategy team members.
• Foster a culture of innovation, collaboration, and continuous learning.
• Support talent development and organizational growth initiatives.
Business Growth
• Support new business opportunities, proposal development, and agency pitches.
• Contribute to thought leadership, industry presentations, and strategic innovation initiatives.
• Identify emerging healthcare trends and market opportunities.
• Drive the development of new capabilities that strengthen Purplemoon and IQVIA's market position.
Qualifications
• Bachelor's degree in Business, Marketing, Life Sciences, Communications, Healthcare Administration, or a related field.
• Advanced degree such as an MBA, MPH, Master's, or PhD preferred.
• 10+ years of experience within pharmaceutical, biotechnology, healthcare consulting, healthcare communications, or healthcare advertising environments.
• Extensive experience in brand strategy, communications planning, commercialization, and product launches.
• Experience supporting rare disease, specialty therapeutics, biotechnology, oncology, or other complex healthcare categories preferred.
• Strong client leadership, presentation, facilitation, and storytelling skills.
• Proven ability to influence senior stakeholders and lead cross-functional teams.
• Exceptional analytical, strategic thinking, and problem-solving capabilities.
Preferred Experience
• Rare disease and specialty pharmaceutical strategy.
• Omnichannel and customer engagement planning.
• Market research and customer insights.
• Launch readiness and commercialization strategy.
• Healthcare advertising or healthcare communications agency experience.
• Global and multi-market pharmaceutical experience.
Success Measures
The successful candidate will:
• Deliver impactful strategic recommendations that drive measurable client and business outcomes.
• Build trusted partnerships with senior pharmaceutical and healthcare stakeholders.
• Successfully lead complex strategic initiatives across multiple client engagements.
• Develop and mentor high-performing strategic talent.
• Contribute to business growth, client retention, and new revenue opportunities.
• Strengthen Purplemoon and IQVIA's reputation as leading partners in healthcare strategy, commercialization, and innovation.
Why Join Purplemoon?
At Purplemoon, you will have the opportunity to work with some of the most innovative organizations in healthcare and life sciences.
Backed by IQVIA's unparalleled data, technology, analytics, and healthcare expertise, we help our clients bring transformative therapies to patients around the world.
We are passionate about collaboration, innovation, and creating work that delivers meaningful impact for clients, healthcare providers, patients, and caregivers.
IQVIA is a leading global provider of clinical research services, commercial insights and healthcare intelligence to the life sciences and healthcare industries. We create intelligent connections to accelerate the development and commercialization of innovative medical treatments to help improve patient outcomes and population health worldwide. Learn more at https://jobs.iqvia.com
IQVIA is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, status as a protected veteran, or any other status protected by applicable law. https://jobs.iqvia.com/eoe

Integration architecture and data movement:

• Interface engines.
• Push and pull architecture.

Clinical areas and projects:

Healthcare security, compliance, and privacy:

• PII/PHI.
• Data encryption in transit and at rest.

• Integration blueprints, interface control documents (ICDs), and data flow diagrams for current and future.
Analytics:

On-prem and cloud migration synchronization:

Why Patients Need You
Everything we do, every day, is driven by an unwavering commitment to the patients, healthcare providers, and customers who depend on us. In Global Commercial Strategy (GCS), we translate science of R&D into value for patients and Pfizer — from early development through launch, growth, and LOE lifecycle. Whether you are defining strategy, managing brands at different lifecycle, or building the capabilities that power our commercial engine, your work directly shapes patient outcomes and the long-term success of Pfizer's portfolio.
Role Summary:
The Senior Manager, Early Commercial Dermatology, Respiratory, and Other Specialty is a key role within the Inflammation & Immunology (I&I) Early Commercial Business, part of the Global Commercial Strategy organization, reporting to the I&I Disease Area Lead. This role will include contributing to long-range commercial strategy, disease-area portfolio prioritization, early commercial assessments, and investment decision support across Dermatology, Respiratory, and Other Specialty priorities within the I&I portfolio.
The broader I&I and Rare Disease portfolio represents significant strategic value to realizing Pfizer's vision to achieve leadership via breakthroughs in prioritized diseases and biological axes, with the goal of generating highly differentiated, multi-indication mega-blockbusters. Today, the portfolio delivers more than $10B globally, with 22 ongoing clinical studies underway to significantly expand the product portfolio over the next several years. This role will help translate that ambition into clear disease-area strategies, disciplined portfolio choices, and integrated commercial plans that maximize patient impact and enterprise value.

• Provide commercial leadership for portfolio prioritization, investment choices, and development opportunities across assigned disease areas.
• Pressure-test commercial assumptions, value drivers, risks, uncertainties, and evidence needs that may influence future launch potential, lifecycle value, and portfolio performance.
• Lead development of executive-ready materials that communicate strategic rationale, opportunity attractiveness, trade-offs, and recommended actions.
• Partner with cross-functional leaders to align on key choices related to indication sequencing, evidence generation, market development, and lifecycle opportunities.

• Lead early commercial assessments for pipeline assets, mechanisms, indications, disease-area opportunities, and potential future product concepts across assigned areas.

Business Development and External Innovation Support:

• Guide assessment of strategic fit, market potential, valuation inputs, competitive scenarios, and portfolio implications for potential external opportunities.
• Partner with Business Development, R&D, GASP, BAI, and Competitive Intelligence colleagues to pressure-test assumptions and identify key decision points.

• Build trusted working relationships across R&D, Medical Affairs, GASP, BAI, Competitive Intelligence, Business Development, and Commercial Regions.
• Foster a culture of enterprise thinking, scientific curiosity, accountability, collaboration, and talent development within the team.
AI-Native Ways of Working:

• Champion use of AI-enabled tools to support scientific and competitive landscape synthesis, market insight generation, scenario development, and decision-support efficiency.

• Use performance insights, stakeholder feedback, and team learnings to continuously improve AI-enabled ways of working across assigned disease areas.
