Job Description:
The Manager – Forward Deployed Engineer AI & Technology Platform is responsible for setting strategic direction and leading a portfolio of AI, data, analytics and digital capabilities supporting Global Development and will be based in either Titusville, NJ or Raritan, NJ.
The Manager operates at the intersection of business strategy, product strategy, engineering, architecture, AI, data and people leadership. The role is accountable for determining which problems should be solved, where technology investments should be made, how capabilities should evolve and how individual products fit into a broader technology strategy.
A core expectation is strategic and critical thinking. The Manager must step back from immediate requests, challenge assumptions, connect decisions across products and organizations and make evidence-based recommendations under ambiguity. The role also requires sufficient hands-on technical depth to challenge architecture, investigate critical issues and prototype emerging capabilities when necessary.
Key Responsibilities
Strategy & Strategic Thinking
· Develop product and technology strategies aligned with Global Development priorities and measurable business outcomes.
· Identify where technology, data, automation and AI can materially improve how work is performed.
· Look beyond individual requests to identify recurring problems, patterns and shared capability needs.
· Determine whether a problem requires new technology, expansion of an existing product, platform reuse, process improvement, consolidation or no additional technology investment.
· Establish multi-year roadmaps balancing immediate needs with long-term platform strategy.
· Anticipate future business and technology needs before they become delivery constraints.
· Translate strategy into priorities, investment recommendations, roadmaps and measurable outcomes.
Critical Thinking & Decision Quality
· Establish the actual problem before committing to a solution and separate symptoms from root causes.
· Identify assumptions within proposals and determine which must be validated before significant investment.
· Constructively challenge business requirements, architecture decisions, timelines and investment proposals when evidence does not support them.
· Develop and evaluate multiple options across business value, user impact, cost, complexity, data readiness, security, scalability, compliance and maintainability.
· Consider second-order consequences across systems, processes, data, teams, users and operating models.
· Make timely decisions under ambiguity while clearly articulating assumptions, evidence, risks and trade-offs.
· Recognize when an initiative should scale, consolidate, pivot, pause or stop.
Portfolio & Investment Leadership
· Own a portfolio of products and technology capabilities aligned to Global Development priorities.
· Prioritize competing initiatives based on business value, strategic alignment, risk, investment and capacity.
· Evaluate build-versus-buy-versus-partner decisions.
· Identify duplicated capabilities, data, integrations, applications or AI investments and drive simplification.
· Determine which capabilities should remain product-specific and which should become reusable platforms or shared services.
· Set criteria for progressing capabilities from experimentation through production and enterprise scale.
· Provide leadership with clear recommendations regarding priorities, investments, risks, dependencies and trade-offs.
AI & Agentic Strategy
· Shape strategic direction for Generative AI, agentic workflows, analytics and intelligent applications.
· Identify workflows where AI can improve decision-making, quality, efficiency or cycle time.
· Separate valuable AI opportunities from technology-driven experimentation.
· Establish reusable architecture and operating patterns rather than allowing disconnected AI implementations to proliferate.
· Define strategic approaches for agents, skills and tools, context, memory, orchestration, semantic capabilities, model routing, evaluation, observability and guardrails.
· Determine where deterministic software, automation, analytics or AI provides the right solution.
· Ensure AI capabilities align with enterprise governance, security, data, validation and production requirements.
Product, Architecture & Engineering Leadership
· Provide direction across product strategy, architecture and engineering execution.
· Establish clear product ownership, technical accountability and decision-making models.
· Ensure teams understand the business problem and intended outcome rather than executing features without context.
· Lead or govern significant architectural decisions affecting multiple products or teams.
· Define principles supporting security, scalability, interoperability, reliability and maintainability.
· Drive reuse across products, APIs, data capabilities, AI components and engineering patterns.
· Ensure short-term delivery decisions do not unnecessarily compromise long-term strategy.
Technical Leadership & Hands-On Depth
· Move directly from business or executive discussions into detailed architecture and engineering conversations.
· Understand and review system architecture, APIs, data flows, semantic architecture and critical implementation decisions.
· Review code or pull requests when needed to understand significant architecture, quality or delivery issues.
· Investigate critical production problems using code, data, logs, traces, metrics and system behavior.
· Prototype emerging AI, agentic, data or integration concepts when hands-on validation is the fastest way to inform a strategic decision.
· Distinguish fundamental technical constraints from solvable engineering problems.
· Evaluate technology options based on business value, architecture, security, interoperability, scalability, maintainability and cost.
· Use AI-assisted development tools to understand codebases, investigate problems and test hypotheses.
Business Partnership & Influence
· Act as a strategic technology partner to Global Development leadership and business stakeholders.
· Translate business strategies into product, data, AI and engineering strategies.
· Bring forward opportunities rather than relying solely on business partners to initiate requests.
· Lead difficult prioritization and trade-off conversations when demand exceeds investment or capacity.
· Translate technical complexity into business value, risk, investment needs and strategic implications.
· Influence senior stakeholders across business, product, engineering, architecture, data, security and enterprise technology.
People & Engineering Organization Leadership
· Build and lead high-performing multidisciplinary product and engineering teams.
· Set expectations for accountability, ownership, technical quality, critical thinking and business understanding.
· Develop Leads and senior engineers capable of independently owning products, architecture and execution.
· Coach teams to understand the why behind their work and consider the broader business and technology landscape.
· Create an environment where assumptions and decisions can be respectfully challenged using evidence.
· Delegate execution while maintaining visibility into strategic decisions and material risks.
· Lead hiring, talent development, succession planning, performance management and capability building.
Delivery, Governance & Transformation
· Maintain accountability for portfolio execution without becoming the day-to-day owner of every delivery decision.
· Establish governance for business outcomes, investment, delivery health, dependencies, technical quality and risk.
· Define appropriate release, validation and production-readiness expectations.
· Intervene when initiatives lose alignment or encounter material cross-organizational or architectural barriers.
· Drive modernization, automation, consolidation and retirement of unnecessary technology.
· Evaluate innovation based on sustainable adoption and measurable outcomes rather than prototypes or novelty.
Technical Skills & Capability Expectations
AI / GenAI
• LLM application architecture
• RAG and semantic retrieval
• Agentic and multi-agent systems
• Agent/tool orchestration and Model Context Protocol
• Context engineering and memory
• Model gateways and routing
• Evaluation, guardrails and human oversight
• AI observability and governance
Data & Intelligence
• SQL and modern enterprise data platforms
• Snowflake or equivalent cloud data platforms
• Relational data architecture
• Semantic layers and metadata
• Knowledge graphs and ontologies
• Vector and document retrieval
• Structured and unstructured data
• Data integration, quality and governance
Software & Integration
• Modern application and service architecture
• Python and API-based architectures
• REST APIs and enterprise integration
• Working understanding of modern web and mobile architecture
• Authentication, SSO and RBAC
• Distributed system and integration patterns
Cloud & Platform
• AWS and Azure architecture
• Containers and Kubernetes
• CI/CD and release engineering
• Configuration and secrets management
• Production monitoring and observability
• Scalable DEV, QA and PROD operating models
Required Experience & Capabilities
· 8+ years of proven experience in engineering with a focus on AI, generative AI, cloud computing, software engineering and automation.
· Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Technology, or a related field.
· Demonstrated leadership of complex product, engineering, data, AI or digital portfolios.
· Strong strategic thinking and ability to connect business objectives to technology strategy.
· Demonstrated critical thinking, including problem framing, root-cause analysis, assumption testing, option evaluation and evidence-based decision-making.
· Ability to make sound decisions under ambiguity and incomplete information.
· Strong working knowledge of enterprise application architecture, cloud, APIs, data platforms, integration and modern engineering practices.
· Experience shaping Generative AI strategies and moving capabilities from experimentation to production.
· Ability to engage technically with architects and engineers while communicating business implications to senior leadership.
· Experience building and developing multidisciplinary product and engineering teams.
· Strong portfolio and investment mindset, including prioritization, value assessment and build-versus-buy decisions.
· Experience operating in regulated or highly governed enterprise environments; life-sciences experience strongly preferred.
What Success Looks Like
· Product and technology investments are clearly connected to Global Development priorities and measurable outcomes.
· Teams solve the right business problems rather than simply delivering requested features.
· Strategic decisions are supported by evidence, explicit assumptions and understood trade-offs.
· Leadership has clear recommendations regarding where investment should increase, decrease, consolidate, pivot or stop.
· AI investments progress from individual experiments toward coherent and reusable capabilities.
· Duplicative technology and unnecessary complexity are progressively reduced.
· Leads and engineering teams operate with increasing independence and accountability.
· Technology improves speed, quality, efficiency, user experience, operating cost or decision-making across Global Development.
Role Differentiator
The Manager is the strategic portfolio and people leader who retains technical credibility: think, decide, enable and go deep when necessary. Success means ensuring the organization solves the right problems at scale.
